- **gooey** (`gooey#1`, cut-off 3) by [sentimental](../../../traits/instructions/sentimental.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve being emotionally moved by tender things like cards, reunions and keepsakes, but gooey stresses sugary, gushing affection while sentimental stresses attachment to mementos and letting fondness sway decisions, so each has aspects the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Gooey is sentimentality carried to a softer, more gushing and sugary degree, while sentimental adds keepsake-keeping and fondness that sways choices; both share the same core of being moved by tender attachment.")

- **gourmet** (`gourmet#1`, cut-off 3) by [epicurean](../../../traits/instructions/epicurean.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a refined, discerning taste for quality, but gourmet is specifically about fine food while epicurean extends to refined pleasures across life generally and emphasizes enjoyment-seeking."), Opus 3 ("Both are refined, discerning appreciation of quality. - **grand** (`grand#1`, cut-off 3) by [dignified](../../../traits/instructions/dignified.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe a composed, poised bearing, but grand stresses stately presence that commands notice while dignified stresses self-respect and avoiding ridicule, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a poised, composed bearing, but grand adds a stately, commanding gravity, a heightened degree of dignity.")

- **gross** (`gross#1`, cut-off 3) by [crude](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve coarse, vulgar behavior, but 'gross' also covers repulsive manners and disregard for others' comfort, while 'crude' centers on vulgar speech and humor, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe coarse, vulgar behaviour. - **grounding** (`grounding#1`, cut-off 3) by [calm](../../../traits/instructions/calm.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve staying steady and de-escalating when others are heated, but grounding adds a practical, unshowy manner and a steadying effect on others, while calm is about temperament."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on a steady, unruffled temperament that settles others in heated moments; grounding adds a practical, down-to-earth manner and puts more weight on the steadying effect on others.")

- **groundling** (`groundling#1`, cut-off 3) by [lowbrow](../../../traits/instructions/lowbrow.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve preferring popular, easy, broad entertainment over refined taste, but groundling also adds rough, unrefined speech and behavior, which lowbrow doesn't imply."), Opus 3 ("Both center on a preference for broad, easy, popular entertainment over refined taste; groundling extends this to rough, unpolished behavior, which is a difference in scope.")

- **grown-up** (`grown_up#1`, cut-off 3) by [middle-aged](../../../traits/instructions/middle_aged.json): Sonnet 2 ("Middle-aged is a specific subset of adulthood (45-65), so it implies being grown-up but is much narrower, while grown-up covers all adults."), Opus 3 ("Middle-aged is a narrower band within adulthood, so it is the same age-status concept with a smaller scope.")
  Gloss: This means being an adult, not a child.
- **gruff** (`gruff#1`, cut-off 3) by [blunt](../../../traits/instructions/blunt.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve saying things directly without softening, but gruff also adds a curt, clipped manner and cutting pleasantries short, while blunt is just directness and honest clarity."), Opus 3 ("Gruff contains bluntness as a core part and adds clipped terseness and curtness, so it is blunt delivery with a harsher, briefer manner.")
  Gloss: This means speaking in short, clipped sentences and cutting pleasantries short, saying what one thinks bluntly and without softening it for anyone's comfort.
- **habitually disparages others** (`habitually_disparages_others#1`, cut-off 3) by [insulting](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve habitually belittling others with cutting speech, but the target includes badmouthing people behind their backs while 'insulting' centers on demeaning the people one is speaking to directly."), Opus 3 ("Both are habitual belittling of people.   Gloss: This means regularly belittling other people and speaking ill of them behind or in front of them, treating their faults as the main thing worth saying about them.
- **habitually manipulates others** (`habitually_manipulates_others#1`, cut-off 4) by [manipulative](../../../traits/instructions/manipulative.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe controlling others through deceit and psychological pressure; 'habitually' only adds a note of frequency, and the other description just lists more tactics."), Opus 4 ("Both describe controlling others' beliefs and choices through deceit and pressure; the target adds habituality but is essentially the same concept.")

- **halfwitted** (`halfwitted#1`, cut-off 3) by [foolish](../../../traits/instructions/foolish.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe poor sense and judgment, but halfwitted stresses poor reasoning and clumsy incomprehension, while foolish stresses missing consequences, not learning from experience and giving bad advice; they share a core with different emphases."), Opus 3 ("Both describe poor sense and poor judgment, though halfwitted stresses weak reasoning and clumsiness while foolish stresses failing to learn from experience and giving misguided advice.")

- **hard to satisfy** (`hard_to_satisfy#1`, cut-off 3) by [perfectionist](../../../traits/instructions/perfectionist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve exacting standards, but 'hard to satisfy' stresses rarely being pleased and pushing others, while 'perfectionist' stresses flawless, meticulous detail; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on exacting standards that are rarely met.   Gloss: This means holding others and oneself to exacting standards, rarely pleased with work or results, and pressing for higher quality even when something is already good enough.
- **hard upon** (`hard_upon#1`, cut-off 3) by [harsh](../../../traits/instructions/harsh.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe severity toward others, but 'hard upon' stresses strict standards and mercilessness while 'harsh' stresses bluntness, quick judgment and cutting replies, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe severity and lack of mercy toward others, and harsh mainly adds a sharper verbal manner on top of the same strict treatment.")
  Gloss: This means dealing harshly with others, holding people to strict standards and showing little mercy when anyone falls short.
- **hard-boiled** (`hard_boiled#1`, cut-off 3) by [cynical](../../../traits/instructions/cynical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both share a cynical view of people, but hard-boiled also includes toughness, dry wit and unsentimental coping, while cynical is only the distrustful view of motives, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Hard-boiled includes a cynical view of people and adds toughness, dry wit and lack of sentiment, so cynicism is a core part of the broader hard-boiled concept.")

- **hard-handed** (`hard_handed#1`, cut-off 3) by [strict](../../../traits/instructions/strict.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve demanding treatment of others with little leniency, but hard-handed stresses harshness and lack of mercy while strict stresses high standards and a pushing philosophy, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe pressing people with unsoftened demands; hard-handed is essentially strictness carried further into harshness and lack of mercy.")
  Gloss: This means treating others with severity, pressing them without softening and holding them to demands that leave little room for mercy or kindness.
- **hard-hearted** (`hard_hearted#1`, cut-off 3) by [uncaring](../../../traits/instructions/uncaring.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve lacking concern for others, but hard-hearted is specifically unmoved by others' suffering, while uncaring is general indifference to how anyone fares, helped or hurt."), Opus 3 ("Both describe indifference to how others fare; uncaring is the broader version, covering welfare in general and one's own actions, while hard-hearted centres on lacking pity for suffering.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's distance from others' suffering, feeling little pity and offering little sympathy when people around one are in pain or need.
- **hard-nosed** (`hard_nosed#1`, cut-off 3) by [data-driven](../../../traits/instructions/data_driven.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both rely on hard evidence over feeling or anecdote, but hard-nosed is a broader unsentimental stance in judging and acting, while data-driven specifically means relying on numbers and statistics."), Opus 3 ("Both mean deciding by evidence rather than sentiment.   Gloss: This means judging matters by hard facts and cold evidence, setting aside sentiment, hopes and appeals to feeling when deciding what is true or what should be done.
- **hare-hearted** (`hare_hearted#1`, cut-off 3) by [cowardly](../../../traits/instructions/cowardly.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve shrinking from danger and confrontation out of fear, but hare-hearted adds jumpiness at noise and sudden movement, while cowardly adds abandoning others when it matters."), Opus 3 ("Both describe shrinking from danger and confrontation out of fear; hare-hearted stresses jumpiness and timidity, while cowardly stresses the moral failure of leaving others to face it.")
  Gloss: This means startling easily at noise or sudden movement and shrinking from danger or confrontation, never willing to face a threat head-on, even when it is small.
- **hare-mad** (`hare_mad#1`, cut-off 3) by [maniacal](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe wild, frenzied behavior as if reason were lost, but hare-mad stresses fast, excitable, fidgety energy while maniacal stresses darker, more extreme intensity like manic laughing and lunging."), Opus 3 ("Both describe wild, frenzied energy that undermines clear thinking, and maniacal is the same quality carried further, to a total loss of reason and self-control.")
  Gloss: This means carrying oneself with a wild, frenzied energy, speaking and moving in fast, excitable bursts as though hardly able to keep still or think straight.
- **hatching** (`hatching#1`, cut-off 4) by [scheming](../../../traits/instructions/scheming.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe secretly devising plans and hiding intentions until execution; scheming adds behind-the-scenes maneuvering but is essentially the same concept."), Opus 4 ("Both describe secretly devising plans and hiding them until execution; scheming adds slight emphasis on behind-the-scenes maneuvering but is essentially interchangeable.")
  Gloss: This means secretly devising schemes in private and keeping one's plans hidden from others until the moment comes to carry them out.
- **hated** (`hated#1`, cut-off 3) by [unpopular](../../../traits/instructions/unpopular.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe poor social standing, but hated involves active contempt and detestation, while unpopular is mere lack of liking and being overlooked; unpopular is milder and passive."), Opus 3 ("Both describe low social regard and exclusion by those around one, with hated being the more intense form, active contempt rather than mere dislike and neglect.")
  Gloss: This means being despised and detested by most of the people around one, held in open contempt and shunned in social settings as a settled part of one's standing.
- **health-conscious eater** (`health_conscious_eater#1`, cut-off 3) by [health-conscious](../../../traits/instructions/health_conscious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve caring about health, but the other is a broad health orientation (checkups, exercise, sleep, doctor visits) that includes eating right as one part, while the target is specifically about diet; neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Health-conscious is the broader concept and includes eating right, so the eater trait is the same concern narrowed to diet.")
  Gloss: This means choosing nutritious, wholesome food as a matter of habit and keeping a steady watch on what goes into one's meals.
- **heartless** (`heartless#1`, cut-off 4) by [callous](../../../traits/instructions/callous.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe cold indifference to others' suffering and feelings; heartless adds inflicting pain without conscience, while callous stresses insensitivity, so they differ only slightly in emphasis."), Opus 4 ("Both describe cold indifference and insensitivity to others' suffering. Heartless adds the absence of pity and conscience, but this is essentially the same concept.")
  Gloss: This means treating others' suffering with cold indifference, feeling no pity for the hurt, and inflicting pain or leaving it unrelieved without any pang of conscience.
- **hearty** (`hearty#1`, cut-off 3) by [friendly](../../../traits/instructions/friendly.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve warmth toward others, but hearty adds booming, expansive, generous exuberance regardless of mood, while friendly is a more general goodwill and approachability without that intensity."), Opus 3 ("Hearty is friendliness turned up into a booming, expansive, relentlessly cheerful manner, so it is the same warm goodwill differing mainly in degree and style.")
  Gloss: This means greeting people with open, booming warmth and keeping one's manner cheerful, generous and expansive in every exchange, whatever the mood of the room.
- **heel** (`heel#1`, cut-off 4) by [treacherous](../../../traits/instructions/treacherous.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe betraying others for personal gain, though 'heel' adds contemptible promise-breaking and 'treacherous' stresses switching sides and selling secrets, so they are nearly the same with slightly different emphasis."), Opus 4 ("Both describe betraying others and switching loyalties for personal gain; they are essentially the same concept, with heel emphasizing contemptibility and broken promises.")
  Gloss: This means behaving with contemptible disloyalty, breaking one's word and betraying others for personal gain, so that no one can rely on one's promises or loyalty.
- **hell-cat** (`hell_cat#1`, cut-off 3) by [quarrelsome (HEXACO)](../../../traits/instructions/quarrelsome_hexaco.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve grudge-holding, readiness to argue and anger, but hell-cat adds fierce spitefulness and picking fights, while the HEXACO trait adds criticalness and stubbornness in arguments."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a grudge-holding, argumentative, quick-to-fight temperament, with hell-cat adding extra fierceness and spite, so it is a more intense degree of the same concept.")

- **heroic** (`heroic#1`, cut-off 3) by [brave](../../../traits/instructions/brave.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve facing danger for others' protection, but heroic stresses self-sacrifice and rescue without hesitation, while brave stresses acting despite fear and covers confrontation; they overlap heavily but each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Heroism is bravery carried further, into selfless protection and rescue of others, so the two share the same core of facing danger for something worth protecting.")
  Gloss: This means facing danger without hesitation and putting one's own safety, comfort, and interests aside when others need protection or rescue.
- **hesitant** (`hesitant#1`, cut-off 3) by [uncertain](../../../traits/instructions/uncertain.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve doubt and holding back, but hesitant centers on pausing and withholding commitment before acting, while uncertain centers on self-doubt and hedging in conviction; each can occur without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe doubt that holds a person back from confident commitment. Uncertain stresses the inner lack of conviction and hedging, while hesitant stresses pausing before acting or speaking.")
  Gloss: This means pausing to doubt before acting or speaking, and holding back from commitment.
- **hidebound** (`hidebound#1`, cut-off 3) by [conservative](../../../traits/instructions/conservative.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both favor established ways over change, but hidebound is a rigid, closed-minded refusal to weigh change, whereas conservative allows gradual change and reasoned preference for stability."), Opus 3 ("Both favor established ways over change, but hidebound is the extreme form: it refuses change outright, while conservative still accepts gradual change.")
  Gloss: This means clinging to established customs and ways of thinking, and treating any proposed change in outlook as something to be refused rather than weighed.
- **high strung** (`high_strung#1`, cut-off 3) by [neurotic (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/neurotic_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve anxiety and emotional reactivity to stress, but the Big Five neuroticism is a much broader trait that also covers sadness, embarrassment, impulsiveness and irritability, while high strung is narrower, about frayed nerves."), Opus 3 ("Neuroticism is a broad trait that includes the anxious, easily rattled reactivity of being high strung, but it adds sadness, self-consciousness and impulsivity, so high strung is a narrower slice of the same concept.")
  Gloss: This means feeling anxious and emotionally reactive, with nerves easily frayed by small disturbances.
- **highfalutin** (`highfalutin#1`, cut-off 3) by [bombastic](../../../traits/instructions/bombastic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve inflated, pompous language meant to impress; highfalutin adds affected airs and pretension to refinement or learning, while bombastic stresses overwhelming grandiosity, so they overlap but each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Both describe inflated, grandiose language meant to impress. - **highly suggestible** (`highly_suggestible#1`, cut-off 4) by [malleable](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe readily changing views and plans under others' influence and pressure; malleable adds loyalties and a stress on forceful speakers, but the core concept is essentially the same."), Opus 4 ("Both describe readily yielding to others' pressure and adopting their views, with malleable adding loyalties, so they are essentially interchangeable.")

- **hircine** (`hircine#1`, cut-off 3) by [lustful](../../../traits/instructions/lustful.json): Sonnet 2 ("Hircine combines lustfulness with a goatlike rank odor, so lustful covers only the desire half and omits the smell; the two share a core but each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Hircine is lustfulness carried to an unchecked, goatish extreme, and it adds a rank odour, so it is mostly the same concept with extra emphasis.")

- **holds to the truth** (`holds_to_the_truth#1`, cut-off 4) by [truthful](../../../traits/instructions/truthful.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both concern refusing to deceive and speaking truly; the other adds accuracy, completeness and correcting misunderstandings, a slight difference in emphasis."), Opus 4 ("Both describe refusing to lie or mislead and speaking only what is true, with only slight differences in emphasis.")

- **holier-than-thou** (`holier_than_thou#1`, cut-off 3) by [judgmental](../../../traits/instructions/judgmental.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve harshly judging others, but holier-than-thou requires assumed moral superiority and self-righteousness, while judgmental is general harsh criticism that need not rest on a sense of one's own virtue."), Opus 3 ("Holier-than-thou is a narrower, moralized form of being judgmental: it is the same harsh judging of others, grounded in assumed moral superiority.")

- **honest and forthright** (`honest_and_forthright#1`, cut-off 4) by [honest](../../../traits/instructions/honest.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe truthfulness and avoiding deception, misleading framing and strategic omission; the 'other' adds acknowledging uncertainty, while the target stresses candor when a softer untruth would be easier, so the difference is slight emphasis."), Opus 4 ("Both describe truthful communication that avoids lies, misleading framing and strategic omission, so they are essentially the same concept, with only slight emphasis differences: forthrightness under pressure versus acknowledging uncertainty.")

- **honest assessment** (`honest_assessment#1`, cut-off 4) by [candid](../../../traits/instructions/candid.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe giving plain, direct judgments of work and ideas, flaws included, without flattery or hedging; 'candid' adds a stance that usefulness matters more than being liked, but the core is the same."), Opus 4 ("Both describe frankly stating one's real judgment of others' work and ideas, flaws included, without inflated praise. - **hotspur** (`hotspur#1`, cut-off 3) by [impulsive](../../../traits/instructions/impulsive.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve acting without weighing consequences, but hotspur adds quick anger and flaring up, while impulsive is broader, covering any urge-driven action without the anger component."), Opus 3 ("Hotspur is a narrower form of impulsiveness, rash action without weighing consequences driven specifically by quick anger, so it implies being impulsive.")

- **humane** (`humane#1`, cut-off 3) by [compassionate](../../../traits/instructions/compassionate.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve caring kindness toward others, but humane stresses gentle, considerate treatment even of difficult or undeserving people, while compassionate stresses empathic sensitivity to suffering; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Humane is defined as compassionate, kind treatment of others.   Gloss: This means treating others with compassion and kindness, giving them consideration and gentleness even when they are difficult, inconvenient, or undeserving of it.
- **humorous** (`humorous#1`, cut-off 3) by [witty](../../../traits/instructions/witty.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve making others laugh with clever humor, but humorous covers acting and general funniness while witty centers on verbal cleverness and wordplay, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Witty is a narrower, verbally clever form of the broader quality of being humorous, so they differ mainly in scope and emphasis.")

- **hygienic** (`hygienic#1`, cut-off 3) by [fastidious](../../../traits/instructions/fastidious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve cleanliness, but hygienic is a steady habit of personal cleanliness, while fastidious adds extreme spotlessness of the home and a strong aversion to grime and germs; each has aspects the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Fastidious is personal cleanliness carried further, to spotlessness and an aversion to germs, and widened to cover the home, so it differs from hygienic in degree and scope.")

- **hyper** (`hyper#1`, cut-off 3) by [manic](../../../traits/instructions/manic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve high energy and fast talking, but manic adds elation, racing ideas, and grandiosity, while hyper is mainly restless overexcitement."), Opus 3 ("Manic contains the hyper core of restless, fast-talking high energy and pushes it further, adding racing ideas, elation and grandiosity.")

- **hypersensual** (`hypersensual#1`, cut-off 3) by [hedonistic](../../../traits/instructions/hedonistic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe pursuing pleasure over restraint, but hypersensual is specifically about excessive bodily and sensory appetites, while hedonistic is a broader orientation toward immediate pleasure over long-term concerns, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe putting pleasure-seeking ahead of restraint and consequence; hypersensual is a more extreme, specifically bodily form of hedonism.")

- **idle-headed** (`idle_headed#1`, cut-off 3) by [foolish](../../../traits/instructions/foolish.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe a lack of sense and foresight in choices, but 'idle-headed' stresses emptiness and thoughtlessness while 'foolish' adds failing to learn from experience and giving misleading advice, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a lack of sense and of foresight about consequences; idle-headed adds a vacant, thoughtless quality, while foolish stresses failing to learn and giving bad advice.")

- **ill-advised** (`ill_advised#1`, cut-off 3) by [foolish](../../../traits/instructions/foolish.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe poor judgment and unwise choices, but foolish adds failing to learn from experience and giving misleading advice, while ill-advised centers on the unwise actions chosen, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on poor judgment about where choices lead; foolish is a broader version that adds not learning from experience and misleading others.")
  Gloss: This means repeatedly making unwise choices and showing poor judgment, choosing courses of action that a sounder mind would have avoided.
- **ill-provided** (`ill_provided#1`, cut-off 3) by [poor](../../../traits/instructions/poor.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe chronic lack of necessities, but 'poor' centers on low income and ownership with specific deprivations, while 'ill-provided' centers on lacking supplies without necessarily implying low income."), Opus 3 ("Both describe chronic material deprivation and going without necessities; poor frames it through low income and housing, while ill-provided stresses the shortage of supplies itself.")

- **illustrious** (`illustrious#1`, cut-off 3) by [famous](../../../traits/instructions/famous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve being widely known, but illustrious adds distinguished achievement and respect, while famous is mere public recognition, even unwanted or without merit."), Opus 3 ("Illustrious is fame carried further, adding high esteem for achievement, while famous is simply being widely known whatever the regard.")

- **impatient** (`impatient#1`, cut-off 3) by [hurried](../../../traits/instructions/hurried.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve urgency and pushing to speed things up, but impatience is restlessness at delay while hurried is a general stance that everything is pressing; each can exist without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both are the same urge to rush rather than wait: impatience is restlessness at delay, and hurriedness is that urgency extended to every matter.")

- **impervious** (`impervious#1`, cut-off 3) by [stoic](../../../traits/instructions/stoic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve keeping composure under emotional pressure, but impervious is specifically being unaffected by criticism or insult, while stoic is broader emotional restraint and philosophical acceptance of any circumstance, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe composure that holds under emotional pressure, but impervious is specifically about being unmoved by criticism or insult, while stoic is a broader calm detachment and acceptance in all circumstances.")
  Gloss: This means staying unmoved when criticized, insulted or wounded, so that one's composure and judgment hold no matter how hard one is pressed emotionally.
- **inalterable** (`inalterable#1`, cut-off 3) by [unyielding](../../../traits/instructions/unyielding.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve holding firm under pressure, but inalterable is about consistent character and convictions across circumstances and moods, while unyielding is specifically refusing to concede ground to others' pushing or pleading."), Opus 3 ("Both describe holding one's stance fixed under pressure; unyielding is the narrower interpersonal case of refusing to give ground to someone pushing or pleading.")

- **inappropriate** (`inappropriate#1`, cut-off 3) by [obscene](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Obscene is a narrower, stronger form of inappropriate speech (sexually crude and shocking), whereas inappropriate also covers any unsuitable remark; they overlap on off-color talk but neither implies the other fully."), Opus 3 ("Both involve unsuitable speech, but inappropriate is broad social unfittingness while obscene is specifically crude sexual lewdness meant to shock; obscene is a narrower, more extreme form that largely implies inappropriateness.")

- **lukewarm** (`lukewarm#1`, cut-off 3) by [apathetic](../../../traits/instructions/apathetic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve lacking enthusiasm and investment, but lukewarm is half-hearted participation while apathetic is a deeper indifference to outcomes and people, with minimal effort."), Opus 3 ("Apathetic is the same lack of engagement as lukewarm, carried further into not caring at all and putting in minimal effort.")

- **lumpish** (`lumpish#1`, cut-off 3) by [slow-witted](../../../traits/instructions/slow_witted.json): Sonnet 2 ("Slow-witted matches only the slow-comprehension part of lumpish, which also includes physical clumsiness and dull conversation, so the two share a core but each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Slow-wittedness is one part of lumpishness, which is broader and also covers physical clumsiness and dull manner, so the two differ mainly in scope.")
  Gloss: This means being clumsy in movement and manner, dull in conversation, and slow to grasp things, with no sharpness or quickness of wit to offset it.
- **lustless** (`lustless#1`, cut-off 3) by [chaste](../../../traits/instructions/chaste.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve absence of sexual desire, but lustless is simply lacking desire while chaste adds purity, moral restraint in speech and thought, and active avoidance of sensual topics."), Opus 3 ("Chaste as described includes being untouched by sexual desire, which is the core of lustless, and adds an emphasis on purity of thought and speech and on turning away from sensual topics.")
  Gloss: This means feeling no sexual desire or appetite at all, so that sex holds no pull and is never something one craves.
- **luxurious** (`luxurious#1`, cut-off 3) by [self-indulgent](../../../traits/instructions/self_indulgent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve habitually gratifying oneself, but luxurious centers on lavish, refined comfort and quality, while self-indulgent centers on yielding to appetites of any kind, including ordinary ones like extra sleep, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe habitually gratifying one's own appetites. Luxurious is that same self-gratification narrowed toward lavish, refined comforts, while self-indulgent covers any indulgence, even a cheap one.")
  Gloss: This means seeking out indulgence and lavish comfort as a matter of course, favoring rich food, fine fabrics and plush surroundings, and treating self-gratification as a central pleasure of one's days.
- **machiavellian** (`machiavellian#1`, cut-off 4) by [Machiavellian (Dark Tetrad)](../../../traits/instructions/machiavellian_dark_tetrad.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe Machiavellianism as scheming, calculated manipulation of others with no regard for those used, with only minor differences in which details are emphasized."), Opus 4 ("Both describe strategic manipulation and deceit to get one's way, with instrumental disregard for others; the Dark Tetrad version adds long-game and reputation emphasis but is the same concept.")
  Gloss: This means scheming to get one's way, deceiving and manipulating others, and treating honesty and loyalty as tools to be used or dropped depending on what they gain.
- **magnificent** (`magnificent#1`, cut-off 3) by [dignified](../../../traits/instructions/dignified.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a dignified bearing, but magnificent adds splendor and commanding grandeur while dignified centers on poise, composure and self-respect, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Magnificent is dignified bearing carried further, into splendid and commanding grandeur, so they share the core of self-respecting poise and differ mainly in degree.")
  Gloss: This means carrying oneself with a splendid, commanding dignity in both manner and character, rising above the ordinary in how one speaks, acts and presents oneself.
- **mainstay** (`mainstay#1`, cut-off 3) by [dependable](../../../traits/instructions/dependable.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both centre on being reliably counted on, but 'mainstay' adds a central, group-holding role while 'dependable' emphasizes following through on commitments, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("A mainstay is dependability carried further into a central role that holds a group together, so it is the same reliability with wider scope.")
  Gloss: This means being the steady, central presence that others count on without fail, holding a group or effort together through consistent reliability over time.
- **majestic** (`majestic#1`, cut-off 3) by [dignified](../../../traits/instructions/dignified.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve poised, composed self-carriage that earns respect, but majestic adds grandeur and stateliness while dignified adds self-respect and avoiding looking ridiculous, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Majestic is a dignified bearing carried further, adding grandeur and stateliness to the same poised self-possession.")
  Gloss: This means carrying oneself with a stately, unhurried dignity, speaking and moving with a grandeur that commands respect without any need to raise one's voice or force the point.
- **malcontented** (`malcontented#1`, cut-off 3) by [discontented](../../../traits/instructions/discontented.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve settled dissatisfaction, but malcontented stresses habitual grumbling and fault-finding that no change relieves, while discontented stresses feeling one's life falls short and wanting more."), Opus 3 ("Both are dissatisfaction with one's lot; malcontented is the chronic, fault-finding, grumbling extreme of the same discontent.")
  Gloss: This means grumbling as a matter of course, finding fault with whatever is at hand, and carrying a settled dissatisfaction that no change of circumstances ever quite relieves.
- **maliciously harmful** (`maliciously_harmful#1`, cut-off 4) by [malevolent](../../../traits/instructions/malevolent.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe wishing for and actively working toward others' suffering out of ill will; malevolent emphasizes underlying hostility while maliciously harmful emphasizes deliberate harm as the goal, which is nearly the same concept."), Opus 4 ("Both describe wishing for and actively working toward others' harm out of ill will; the target stresses deliberately hurting with pain as the goal, a nearly identical concept.")
  Gloss: This means wanting others to suffer and deliberately setting out to hurt them, treating their pain as the goal rather than an unfortunate side effect of one's actions.
- **man-keen** (`man_keen#1`, cut-off 3) by [passionate](../../../traits/instructions/passionate.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve visible enthusiasm and investment, but 'passionate' adds intensity, strong emotion and deep commitment, while 'man-keen' is more about eager, energetic engagement with whatever is at hand."), Opus 3 ("Both describe enthusiasm for what one is engaged in, but passionate adds intense emotion and deep commitment, a stronger degree of the same eagerness.")
  Gloss: This means approaching tasks and conversations with visible eagerness, showing real enthusiasm for what is in front of one and pursuing it with energy and interest.
- **manipulable** (`manipulable#1`, cut-off 4) by [malleable](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe readily yielding opinions and choices to others' pressure with little firm position of one's own; the only differences are minor emphasis (flattery vs. forcefulness, loyalties)."), Opus 4 ("Both describe readily yielding one's opinions and choices to others' pressure with little resistance of one's own, so either label could stand for the other.")
  Gloss: This means readily letting one's opinions and choices be shifted by whatever others argue, press, or flatter one into, with little resistance of one's own.
- **masking** (`masking#1`, cut-off 3) by [repressed](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve keeping feelings from showing, but masking is a composed outward concealment while repressed is an inward holding-in or suppression of the feelings; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe keeping one's feelings hidden from others; repressed stresses the strain of holding them in, while masking stresses the composed outward facade.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's true feelings hidden behind a composed, unreadable surface, so that others rarely see what one is actually experiencing.
- **masks feelings** (`masks_feelings#1`, cut-off 3) by [reserved](../../../traits/instructions/reserved.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve keeping feelings hidden from others, but 'reserved' also adds polite distance and not verbalizing personal matters, while 'masks feelings' stresses concealing the outward display (face, voice) as well as words."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on keeping one's feelings hidden; reserved widens this to a general polite distance from others, so it differs mainly in scope.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's emotions hidden from others as a settled habit, so that feelings rarely show in one's face, voice, or words even when one is hurt, afraid, or happy.
- **maudlin** (`maudlin#1`, cut-off 3) by [self-pitying](../../../traits/instructions/self_pitying.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve wallowing in one's own hurts, but maudlin adds tearful sentimentality and nostalgia for past losses, while self-pitying centers on perceived unfairness and seeking sympathy; each lacks what the other adds."), Opus 3 ("Maudlin is essentially self-pity with a tearful, sentimental, nostalgic emphasis, so it sits within the same concept as self-pitying, differing mainly in flavour and emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means dwelling on one's own hurts with tearful sentimentality, lingering over past losses and wallowing in self-pity rather than moving on or keeping a steady composure.
- **mawkish** (`mawkish#1`, cut-off 3) by [sentimental](../../../traits/instructions/sentimental.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve tender emotion, but mawkish is excessive, cloying overexpression of sentiment, while sentimental is a fondness for keepsakes and nostalgia that sways choices, without implying excess or syrupy display."), Opus 3 ("Mawkish is sentimentality carried to an excessive, cloying degree, so the two differ mainly in degree.")
  Gloss: This means feeling and expressing everything through syrupy, overwrought sentiment, pressing tender emotions far past what the moment warrants and dwelling on them maudlinly.
- **methodical and orderly** (`methodical_and_orderly#1`, cut-off 3) by [methodical](../../../traits/instructions/methodical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve working step by step in a systematic sequence, but the target also includes keeping materials and surroundings orderly, while the other adds sticking to a plan under surprises; the shared core is systematic work."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on systematic, step-by-step working; the target is broader, adding an orderly arrangement of materials and surroundings, so the difference is one of scope.")
  Gloss: This means working through tasks in a systematic sequence and keeping one's materials, notes and surroundings in a consistent, orderly arrangement so that nothing is left to chance or memory.
- **militarist** (`militarist#1`, cut-off 3) by [hawkish](../../../traits/instructions/hawkish.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both favor military force in policy, but hawkish is a more aggressive stance on resolving conflicts (striking first, scorning negotiation), while militarist is a broader belief in military strength guiding policy."), Opus 3 ("Both center on favoring military force in policy. Hawkish is a more aggressive, conflict-focused version of the militarist belief that force should guide policy.")
  Gloss: This means believing that military force and strength should guide policy.
- **misanthropist** (`misanthropist#1`, cut-off 3) by [cynical](../../../traits/instructions/cynical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a settled distrust of human motives, but misanthropy adds active dislike of human company, while cynicism is about pessimistic belief in self-interest without necessarily disliking people."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on a settled distrust of people's motives, but misanthropy carries it further into active dislike of human company.")
  Gloss: This means holding a settled distrust of people in general, expecting the worst of others' motives and regarding most human company with dislike rather than warmth.
- **mistrustful** (`mistrustful#1`, cut-off 3) by [cynical](../../../traits/instructions/cynical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve assuming others act from self-interest, but mistrustful is a wary stance toward particular people until they prove themselves, while cynical is a broader pessimistic view of human nature."), Opus 3 ("Both presume others act from self-interest rather than good faith; cynical extends this distrust into a broader pessimistic view of human nature.")
  Gloss: This means doubting that others are acting in good faith, and presuming that their words and favors hide self-interest or deceit until they have proved otherwise.
- **moldable** (`moldable#1`, cut-off 4) by [malleable](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe readily yielding one's opinions to others' pressure; malleable adds plans and loyalties and a slightly broader scope, but the core concept is the same."), Opus 4 ("Both describe readily yielding one's opinions to others' pressure; malleable adds plans and loyalties but is essentially the same concept.")
  Gloss: This means yielding readily to the views and pressures of others, letting one's own opinions bend and reshape whenever someone pushes back on them.
- **monosyllabic** (`monosyllabic#1`, cut-off 3) by [concise](../../../traits/instructions/concise.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve brevity in speech, but monosyllabic means curt, clipped replies that withhold elaboration and pleasantries, while concise means efficiently conveying a full core message; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe brevity without elaboration; monosyllabic is a more extreme, clipped form that also drops pleasantries.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's replies short and clipped, answering in a word or a few terse phrases rather than offering explanation, elaboration, or pleasantries.
- **morally flexible** (`morally_flexible#1`, cut-off 4) by [expedient](../../../traits/instructions/expedient.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe dropping moral principles whenever it benefits oneself; 'expedient' adds an emphasis on ease and immediate payoff, but the core concept is essentially the same."), Opus 4 ("Both describe abandoning moral principles when they become costly or inconvenient for personal gain; expedient adds a slight emphasis on immediate ease, but the concept is essentially the same.")
  Gloss: This means setting aside one's ethical principles whenever bending them serves one's own convenience, treating right and wrong as negotiable depending on what one stands to gain.
- **motiveless** (`motiveless#1`, cut-off 3) by [aimless](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve lacking purpose, but motiveless means no drive or reason behind actions, while aimless means lacking long-term goals or direction; one could have momentary motives yet be aimless, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a lack of purpose. Motiveless is the more extreme form, with no want or reason behind any act, while aimless means lacking life goals and direction.")
  Gloss: This means having no drive or reason for acting, so that nothing one does arises from wanting anything or having any purpose behind it.
- **multi-disciplinary** (`multi_disciplinary#1`, cut-off 3) by [generalist](../../../traits/instructions/generalist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve drawing on multiple fields, but multi-disciplinary stresses actively combining disciplines on a problem, while generalist stresses broad knowledge as opposed to specialization; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe drawing on and connecting several fields. Generalist stresses broad knowledge and versatility as a disposition, while multi-disciplinary stresses applying several fields to a problem, so they differ mainly in emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means drawing on several fields of expertise at once, moving between disciplines to approach a problem from more than one body of knowledge.
- **mundane** (`mundane#1`, cut-off 3) by [prosaic](../../../traits/instructions/prosaic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe plain, unflamboyant manner, but mundane covers any workaday style in speech, thought or tasks, while prosaic is specifically matter-of-fact, unpoetic expression, so they share a core and each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a plain, unadorned manner lacking flair. Prosaic narrows this to matter-of-fact expression without poetry or imagery, so it is the same concept with a narrower scope and different emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's manner plain and workaday, showing no flair, drama or distinctive flourish in how one speaks, thinks or handles any task.
- **mushy** (`mushy#1`, cut-off 3) by [sentimental](../../../traits/instructions/sentimental.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve tender, easily stirred feeling toward people and places, but mushy stresses effusive gushing in reactions while sentimental stresses keepsakes, tearing up and fondness swaying choices, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe tender fondness for people and places. Mushy stresses effusive, gushing display, while sentimental stresses attachment to keepsakes and memories, so they share a core with different emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means feeling things loudly and tenderly, letting sentiment spill into every reaction and warming easily to the point of gushing over people, places and small kindnesses.
- **naturalistic** (`naturalistic#1`, cut-off 3) by [materialist](../../../traits/instructions/materialist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both reject the supernatural, but naturalistic is specifically about causal explanation while materialist adds reductive dismissal of abstract, emotional and subjective phenomena; a naturalist need not be a reductive materialist, and vice versa in emphasis."), Opus 3 ("Materialism as described is a stronger version of naturalism: it also rejects the spiritual, and it further reduces abstractions, emotions and subjective experience to the physical.")
  Gloss: This means holding that only natural causes operate in the world, so that one rejects any supernatural agency or explanation for events.
- **ne'er-do-well** (`neer_do_well#1`, cut-off 3) by [lazy](../../../traits/instructions/lazy.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve idleness and avoiding effort, but ne'er-do-well adds aimlessness and lack of purpose or contribution, while lazy is specifically about avoiding effort and doing the bare minimum; neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("A ne'er-do-well is essentially laziness extended to a whole life: idle, shiftless and without ambition, where lazy covers avoiding effort on tasks.")

- **neat** (`neat#1`, cut-off 3) by [organized](../../../traits/instructions/organized.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve keeping things in order so they're findable, but neat centers on tidiness of spaces and belongings, while organized adds systems, labeling, and time planning; either can exist without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe keeping one's things in order so nothing is lost; organized extends the same orderliness to time and planning, a difference mainly of scope.")
  Gloss: This means keeping every space and belonging in order, putting things back where they go, and arranging one's surroundings, papers, and plans so that everything is tidy and easy to find.
- **nebulous** (`nebulous#1`, cut-off 3) by [vague](../../../traits/instructions/vague.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve lack of definiteness, but nebulous covers hazy thinking, manner and unsettled plans, while vague is specifically about imprecise, non-committal language; they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a lack of definite, specific shape. Nebulous covers hazy thinking and manner broadly, while vague focuses on non-specific language, so they differ mainly in scope.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's thinking hazy and one's manner indistinct, never settling ideas, plans or positions into a clear, definite shape.
- **neoteric** (`neoteric#1`, cut-off 3) by [early-adopter](../../../traits/instructions/early_adopter.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both favor the new over the old, but neoteric is a general outlook and taste for current ideas and styles, while early-adopter is specifically about quickly taking up new products or methods as they come out; neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Both are a preference for the new over the old; early-adopter is a narrower, more extreme form focused on immediately taking up new products and methods.")

- **no-nonsense** (`no_nonsense#1`, cut-off 3) by [concise](../../../traits/instructions/concise.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve brief, direct communication without padding, but no-nonsense adds a brisk, businesslike tone that drops pleasantries and emotion, while concise is only about brevity and omitting unneeded detail; either can occur without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe brief, direct speech that cuts unneeded material; no-nonsense goes further by also stripping out pleasantries and emotion for a brisk, businesslike tone.")
  Gloss: This means speaking in short, direct sentences, cutting straight to the point, and keeping exchanges brisk and businesslike without pleasantries, padding, or emotional embellishment.
- **non-chalant** (`non_chalant#1`, cut-off 3) by [unflappable](../../../traits/instructions/unflappable.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe staying calm under pressure, but nonchalant adds a lack of concern or excitement about outcomes, while unflappable stresses composure and keeping the thread, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe staying calm and unrattled under pressure; nonchalant adds an air of indifference and no excitement, while unflappable stresses keeping composure.")

- **nonconforming** (`nonconforming#1`, cut-off 3) by [individualistic](../../../traits/instructions/individualistic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both favor personal choice over group norms, but nonconforming is about openly departing from customs, while individualistic also includes self-reliance and autonomy, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on putting one's own way ahead of group norms.   Gloss: This means choosing one's own way of dressing, speaking and living over the customs and expectations that others around one follow, without apologizing for departing from them.
- **nonexplosive** (`nonexplosive#1`, cut-off 3) by [unflappable](../../../traits/instructions/unflappable.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve staying calm under pressure, but nonexplosive is specifically about not flaring into anger, while unflappable is broader composure against surprise and fluster without being anger-specific."), Opus 3 ("Both describe staying composed under pressure, but unflappable is the broader quality, covering surprise and fluster, while nonexplosive covers only anger and outbursts.")

- **nonfunctional** (`nonfunctional#1`, cut-off 3) by [incompetent](../../../traits/instructions/incompetent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe failing at one's intended job, but 'nonfunctional' is about uselessness or lack of working value (applicable even to things), while 'incompetent' is about lacking skill and fumbling; they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe failing at one's job, but incompetent narrows it to lacking the know-how and botching the work despite trying, whereas nonfunctional covers any such failure.")

- **nonirritable** (`nonirritable#1`, cut-off 3) by [even-tempered](../../../traits/instructions/even_tempered.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve staying calm and unruffled, but nonirritable is about patience with frustrations and other people, while even-tempered is about emotional consistency across good and bad days, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Even-tempered is a broader steadiness of mood across good and bad news, which includes the specific calm under frustration that nonirritable describes.")

- **nonpersistent** (`nonpersistent#1`, cut-off 3) by [defeatist](../../../traits/instructions/defeatist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve giving up when things get difficult, but defeatist adds a pessimistic expectation of failure and permanent abandonment, while nonpersistent is simply a lack of perseverance without necessarily that outlook."), Opus 3 ("Defeatism includes giving up at the first setback, which is nonpersistence. - **nymphomaniacal** (`nymphomaniacal#1`, cut-off 3) by [lustful](../../../traits/instructions/lustful.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern strong sexual desire, but nymphomaniacal stresses insatiable, excessive compulsive pursuit while lustful stresses expressed desire and sexualizing conversation, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe strong sexual desire, and nymphomaniacal is the same appetite taken to an insatiable, compulsive extreme.")

- **objectionable** (`objectionable#1`, cut-off 3) by [rude](../../../traits/instructions/rude.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve offensive, impolite conduct toward others, but 'objectionable' is broader (coarse, repugnant, insulting) while 'rude' is specifically discourteous manners, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Rudeness is a narrower, milder form of the offensive, unpleasant conduct that objectionable describes, which adds coarseness and repugnance.")

- **offensive** (`offensive#1`, cut-off 3) by [rude](../../../traits/instructions/rude.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve discourteous behavior toward others, but the target is deliberate, insulting and enjoys wounding, while the other is a broader lack of manners and sharp tone without necessarily intending harm."), Opus 3 ("Both describe discourteous treatment of others, but offensive carries rudeness further into deliberate insult and pleasure in wounding, while rude is the broader everyday lack of courtesy.")

- **offers fresh perspectives** (`offers_fresh_perspectives#1`, cut-off 3) by [creative](../../../traits/instructions/creative.json): Sonnet 2 ("Creative includes presenting novel perspectives, which is the core of offering fresh perspectives, but it also covers imaginative solutions and original methods, so it is broader and neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Creative explicitly includes presenting novel perspectives but extends to imaginative solutions and original methods generally, so the target is a narrower facet of it.")

- **old fashioned** (`old_fashioned#1`, cut-off 3) by [conservative](../../../traits/instructions/conservative.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both favor established ways over new ones, but 'conservative' adds a focus on stability and gradual change in systems, while 'old fashioned' stresses style and taste, so they share a core without being the same."), Opus 3 ("Both mean preferring the established over the new; old-fashioned stresses styles and tastes, while conservative stresses stability and resistance to reform, so they differ only in emphasis.")

- **one of many** (`one_of_many#1`, cut-off 3) by [plain-looking](../../../traits/instructions/plain_looking.json): Sonnet 2 ("Plain-looking covers only the unremarkable-appearance part of 'one of many', which also includes manner and circumstance, so they overlap but neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Plain-looking is the appearance part of being one of many, a narrower version of the same unremarkableness that leaves out manner and circumstance.")

- **one-sided** (`one_sided#1`, cut-off 3) by [partisan](../../../traits/instructions/partisan.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve backing one side and giving the other little fair weight, but partisan is specifically political, loyal to a side's line, and assumes bad faith, while one-sided can apply to any dispute without group loyalty."), Opus 3 ("Partisan is one-sidedness carried further and narrowed to political controversies, with added loyalty to a group line, so it is the same core concept differing in scope and degree.")

- **open to new experiences** (`open_to_new_experiences#1`, cut-off 3) by [adventurous](../../../traits/instructions/adventurous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve embracing unfamiliar foods, places and plans, but openness stresses learning and receptivity to ideas while adventurousness stresses thrill-seeking and restlessness with routine, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe readily embracing unfamiliar foods, places and things. - **openly joyful** (`openly_joyful#1`, cut-off 3) by [effusive](../../../traits/instructions/effusive.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve unrestrained outward expression of positive feeling, but 'openly joyful' is specifically about happiness and warmth while 'effusive' stresses overflowing, excessive enthusiasm of any kind, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe unrestrained expression of positive enthusiasm; effusive is essentially the same open delight carried to overflowing excess.")

- **orderly and tidy** (`orderly_and_tidy#1`, cut-off 3) by [organized](../../../traits/instructions/organized.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both are about keeping things and tasks in systematic order, but 'orderly and tidy' stresses physical neatness and routine while 'organized' stresses systems and planning of time, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe keeping things systematically in their place and following a method. Tidy stresses neat arrangement, while organized stresses filing and time planning, so they differ mainly in emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's space, belongings, and work neatly arranged, following a methodical routine, putting each thing in its place, and finishing tasks in a clear, set order.
- **ornery** (`ornery#1`, cut-off 3) by [disagreeable](../../../traits/instructions/disagreeable.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe a contrary, quarrelsome and hard-to-get-along-with temperament, but ornery stresses irritable grumbling and a sour outlook, while disagreeable stresses open contradiction and indifference to keeping the peace."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a contrary, hard-to-get-along-with disposition.
