- **otiose** (`otiose#1`, cut-off 3) by [lazy](../../../traits/instructions/lazy.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve unproductiveness, but otiose is contentedly idle and purposeless, while lazy is habitual effort-avoidance and doing the bare minimum; neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe avoiding effort and productive work; otiose is a more complete, contented idleness, so it is essentially laziness carried further.")
  Gloss: This means spending one's days idle and unproductive, accomplishing nothing useful and happily letting time pass without any purpose or productive aim.
- **outgoing** (`outgoing#1`, cut-off 3) by [extraverted (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/extraverted_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both share sociable warmth and readily engaging with people, but Big Five extraversion is broader, adding assertiveness, activity level and excitement-seeking, while outgoing centres on friendly, talkative manner."), Opus 3 ("Outgoing is the sociable, warm-talker core of extraversion, while the Big Five trait is broader and also covers assertiveness, activity, excitement-seeking and cheerfulness.")
  Gloss: This means approaching people with easy warmth, starting conversations readily, and filling silences with talk, so that one's manner in company is open, friendly and animated.
- **over-analytic** (`over_analytic#1`, cut-off 3) by [analytical](../../../traits/instructions/analytical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve breaking things down through analysis, but 'over-analytic' adds excessive, paralysing deliberation and distrust of instinct, while 'analytical' is a neutral, often positive methodical reasoning style."), Opus 3 ("Over-analytic is the analytical habit of systematic breakdown carried to excess, to the point of distrusting instinct and delaying decisions.")
  Gloss: This means dissecting every choice at length and trusting analysis over gut feeling, so that one rarely acts on instinct and keeps reconsidering decisions long after they could have been made.
- **over-anxious** (`over_anxious#1`, cut-off 3) by [neurotic (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/neurotic_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve fretting about what could go wrong, but neuroticism is much broader, adding irritability, sadness, embarrassment, impulsiveness and stress collapse, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Over-anxious worry is the anxiety facet of Big Five neuroticism, which is broader and also covers anger, sadness, self-consciousness, impulsiveness and stress vulnerability, so the two differ mainly in scope.")
  Gloss: This means worrying about nearly everything as a matter of course, imagining what could go wrong in each plan and conversation, and finding it hard to settle even when things are going well.
- **over-optimistic** (`over_optimistic#1`, cut-off 3) by [optimistic](../../../traits/instructions/optimistic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve hopeful expectations, but over-optimistic means unrealistic hope that persists against the evidence, while optimistic is a general positive focus without that distortion, so the former is the excessive form of the latter."), Opus 3 ("Over-optimistic is optimism carried past what the evidence supports, so it is the same hopeful outlook to a greater degree.")
  Gloss: This means expecting that things will work out better than the evidence supports, and carrying on with that hope even when the signs point the other way.
- **overactive** (`overactive#1`, cut-off 3) by [manic](../../../traits/instructions/manic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve relentless high energy and fast talking, but manic adds elation, racing ideas and grandiosity, while overactive is just excess restless pace."), Opus 3 ("Manic covers overactive's restless, fast, constant high-energy pace and pushes it further, adding elation and grandiosity, so it is essentially an intensified form of the same concept.")
  Gloss: This means keeping up a restless, high-energy pace in one's behaviour, moving, talking and reacting faster and more constantly than the situation calls for, and never settling into stillness.
- **overambitious** (`overambitious#1`, cut-off 3) by [ambitious](../../../traits/instructions/ambitious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve setting high goals, but overambitious is about unrealistic goals pursued despite lacking means, while ambitious is about drive to rise and never settling; ambitious doesn't imply unrealism, and overambitious doesn't require status-climbing."), Opus 3 ("Overambitious is ambition carried past the point of realism, so both describe setting high goals, differing mainly in degree.")
  Gloss: This means setting goals for oneself that stretch well past what is realistic or achievable, and pressing on toward them even when the time, resources and ability to reach them are plainly lacking.
- **overdone** (`overdone#1`, cut-off 3) by [theatrical](../../../traits/instructions/theatrical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve exaggerated, stagey expression, but 'overdone' stresses excess beyond what the moment calls for, while 'theatrical' stresses dramatic flair and commanding presence, which can be deliberate and appropriate."), Opus 3 ("Both describe exaggerated, stage-like expression; overdone stresses that it exceeds what the moment calls for, while theatrical stresses dramatic performance flair.")
  Gloss: This means pushing every gesture, phrase and reaction past what the moment calls for, turning ordinary expression into theatrical exaggeration.
- **overearnest** (`overearnest#1`, cut-off 3) by [earnest](../../../traits/instructions/earnest.json): Sonnet 2 ("Overearnest is an excessive, rigid form of earnestness, but earnest as described stresses sincerity and not mocking, without the inability to relax or the treating of small things as weighty."), Opus 3 ("Overearnest is earnest sincerity and seriousness carried to excess, unable to relax into lightness, so it is the same concept differing in degree.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's manner so intensely eager and solemn that one cannot relax into lightness, treating every small exchange as though it carried great weight.
- **overfierce** (`overfierce#1`, cut-off 3) by [aggressive](../../../traits/instructions/aggressive.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve hostile, combative force in conflict, but overfierce stresses excessive, temper-driven intensity while aggressive stresses goal-driven confrontation and rejecting compromise, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe hostile, combative force in conflict. Overfierce is the argumentative, hot-tempered and excessive form of the confrontational pushing that aggressive names.")
  Gloss: This means meeting every disagreement with hostile force, pressing arguments harder and sharper than the moment calls for, and showing a temper that is always close to the edge of attack.
- **overkind** (`overkind#1`, cut-off 3) by [generous](../../../traits/instructions/generous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve giving to others, but overkind is excessive kindness that stops helping, while generous is freely giving resources and carries no implication of excess or harm; they overlap in giving but each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Overkind is giving kindness and generosity carried past the sensible point, so it is the same giving disposition as generous taken to excess.")
  Gloss: This means giving kindness, consideration and generosity in excess of what is sensible, past the point where they still help the person receiving them.
- **overneat** (`overneat#1`, cut-off 3) by [organized](../../../traits/instructions/organized.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve order, but overneat is a rigid, compulsive tidiness about objects and surfaces, while organized is a functional system for things and time without the rigidity or distress about disarray."), Opus 3 ("Both are about keeping things and routines in order. Overneat carries this to a rigid, anxious extreme that treats any disarray as a personal failing, while organized is the functional, systematic version.")
  Gloss: This means keeping every object, surface and routine in rigid order, and treating any slight disarray as a personal failing to be corrected at once.
- **overnice** (`overnice#1`, cut-off 3) by [uptight](../../../traits/instructions/uptight.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve fussing over small details and insisting things be done exactly right, but uptight adds tension, rigidity and unease for others, while overnice is focused on excessive precision."), Opus 3 ("Both are about fussing that small things be done exactly right, but uptight adds tension, rigidity and putting others on edge, so it is the same core carried with extra emotional emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means fussing over small details and insisting that everything be exactly right, even when the difference hardly matters to anyone else.
- **overpartial** (`overpartial#1`, cut-off 3) by [sectarian](../../../traits/instructions/sectarian.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve favoring one's own group over others, but sectarian is specifically about religious in-group loyalty and indifference to outsiders, while overpartial is general unfair side-taking that skews judgment toward any party."), Opus 3 ("Sectarian is a specific case of partiality: favoring one's own faith group over others, so it is narrower in scope than general overpartiality.")
  Gloss: This means taking sides too readily, favoring one party or group over others without fair cause and letting loyalty to them tilt one's judgment, advice and treatment of everyone else.
- **overrides guidance freely** (`overrides_guidance_freely#1`, cut-off 4) by [rule-breaking](../../../traits/instructions/rule_breaking.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe habitually setting aside rules and instructions when they are inconvenient; rule-breaking adds the bending of procedures and the 'ask forgiveness' attitude, but the core is essentially the same."), Opus 4 ("Both describe habitually brushing aside rules and instructions whenever they get in the way, with only trivial differences in wording.")
  Gloss: This means brushing aside rules and instructions whenever they get in the way, as a settled habit of character rather than a rare lapse.
- **overrigorous** (`overrigorous#1`, cut-off 3) by [perfectionist](../../../traits/instructions/perfectionist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve very high exacting standards, but overrigorous stresses excess beyond need and harsh treatment of lapses in others, while perfectionist stresses flawlessness and meticulousness without implying excess or severity."), Opus 3 ("Both are about holding exceptionally high, exacting standards; overrigorous stresses that the standards exceed what is needed, are imposed on others too, and treat lapses harshly, making it perfectionism carried further.")
  Gloss: This means insisting on exacting standards from oneself and others far beyond what the work actually requires, and treating every lapse as a serious failing.
- **oversentimental** (`oversentimental#1`, cut-off 3) by [sentimental](../../../traits/instructions/sentimental.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve tender emotionality, but oversentimental is excessive, inflated emotion out of proportion to events, while sentimental is a fondness for keepsakes and nostalgia that stays within normal bounds, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Oversentimental is sentimentality carried to excess, the same tender emotionality pushed further past what situations warrant.")
  Gloss: This means treating every moment as an occasion for tears, letting emotion run far past what a situation calls for and swelling each feeling into something grander than it is.
- **oversevere** (`oversevere#1`, cut-off 3) by [harsh](../../../traits/instructions/harsh.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve severity toward others, but oversevere centers on unbending standards and harsh treatment of mistakes, while harsh adds bluntness and cutting replies, so each includes something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe severity and quick, unforgiving judgment of people; harsh puts more weight on a cutting, unsoftened manner, while oversevere stresses rigid standards that make no allowance for circumstance.")
  Gloss: This means judging others by unbending standards and treating their mistakes harshly, with little allowance for circumstance, effort or human weakness.
- **overstrung** (`overstrung#1`, cut-off 3) by [neurotic (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/neurotic_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve poor emotional stability and tension under stress, but neuroticism is a much broader cluster (worry, irritability, sadness, shyness, impulsiveness) while overstrung is specifically jumpy, taut nerves."), Opus 3 ("Overstrung is a narrow facet of nervous tension and jumpiness, while Big Five neuroticism is a broad negative-emotionality trait that takes in that tension along with anger, sadness, self-consciousness and impulsivity.")
  Gloss: This means being tense and jumpy by temperament, startling easily and keeping one's nerves stretched taut through ordinary situations that other people take in stride.
- **owlish** (`owlish#1`, cut-off 3) by [solemn](../../../traits/instructions/solemn.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both share a grave, weighty, formal manner, but owlish adds a studious, wise-looking deliberateness while solemn adds rarely joking and uniform sobriety, so each has features the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Owlish is essentially solemn gravity with an added studious, wise-looking flavour, so it is a narrower, specialised form of solemnity.")
  Gloss: This means carrying oneself with a grave, solemn air, speaking deliberately and looking studious or wise, as though every remark were weighed before it is offered.
- **owns its values** (`owns_its_values#1`, cut-off 3) by [postconventional (Kohlberg)](../../../traits/instructions/postconventional_kohlberg.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve self-derived convictions rather than borrowed ones, but postconventional is specifically about universal rights and justice principles independent of group authority, while owning values applies to any convictions and doesn't require that independence from groups or a justice focus."), Opus 3 ("Both describe reasoning out one's own principles rather than adopting them from others or a group; postconventional is narrower, covering justice and rights, and stresses validity independent of group authority.")
  Gloss: This means holding one's convictions as one's own, having reasoned them through and settled on them, rather than repeating principles absorbed from others or adopted to fit in.
- **pachydermatous** (`pachydermatous#1`, cut-off 3) by [unflappable](../../../traits/instructions/unflappable.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve staying composed under pressure, but pachydermatous is specifically about shrugging off criticism and insults, while unflappable covers composure against any surprise or setback."), Opus 3 ("Both describe composure that holds under pressure. Thick-skinned composure is limited to criticism and insults, while unflappable extends the same composure to surprises and setbacks.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's composure when criticized or slighted, shrugging off insults and barbs without visible hurt, and remaining unbothered by remarks that would wound a more sensitive person.
- **padding** (`padding#1`, cut-off 3) by [verbose](../../../traits/instructions/verbose.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve excess wordiness, but padding is specifically filler and redundancy adding nothing new, while verbose is broader long-windedness that can include real elaboration and detail."), Opus 3 ("Padding is a narrower form of verbosity: excess length made of empty filler, whereas verbose also covers excessive but substantive elaboration.")
  Gloss: This means stretching every point with filler phrases and redundant wording that add bulk to one's answers while saying nothing new.
- **pansy** (`pansy#1`, cut-off 3) by [cowardly](../../../traits/instructions/cowardly.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve lacking nerve and shrinking from conflict, but 'pansy' adds being mocked as soft or effeminate, while 'cowardly' centres on fear and abandoning others in danger."), Opus 3 ("Pansy is essentially cowardice, a lack of nerve and flinching from conflict, narrowed to men and given a derisive slant of softness or effeminacy.")
  Gloss: This means being a man who lacks nerve and backbone, flinching from conflict and hardship, and who is mocked as soft or effeminate.
- **pappy** (`pappy#1`, cut-off 3) by [parent](../../../traits/instructions/parent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve being a parent, but 'pappy' is specifically being a father addressed by that name, while 'parent' is the broader role of raising children with its daily burdens, so one is a narrower case of the other."), Opus 3 ("Being a father called Pappy is a narrower, gendered case of being a parent with children, so the two differ mainly in scope.")
  Gloss: This means being someone's father, addressed as Pappy.
- **party-loving** (`party_loving#1`, cut-off 3) by [extraverted (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/extraverted_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve enjoying lively social settings, but extraversion is a much broader trait (assertiveness, activity, warmth, excitement-seeking) while party-loving is specifically about enjoying parties and crowds, so each has content the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Party-loving is a narrow form of extraversion, centred on its sociability and excitement-seeking side, while extraversion also covers assertiveness, activity and positive emotion.")
  Gloss: This means enjoying parties and lively social gatherings, seeking out the crowd, the music and the buzz of a full room, and coming alive when a night is in full swing.
- **passionless** (`passionless#1`, cut-off 3) by [dispassionate](../../../traits/instructions/dispassionate.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve emotional detachment and an unmoved manner, but dispassionate emphasizes objectivity and neutrality while passionless emphasizes lack of warmth and enthusiasm, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe emotional detachment and an unmoved manner. Dispassionate leans toward objectivity and neutrality, while passionless leans toward a lack of warmth and enthusiasm, so they differ mainly in emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's manner even and unmoved, showing little warmth, enthusiasm or feeling toward people, projects or events, and treating emotional displays as beside the point.
- **patient** (`patient#1`, cut-off 3) by [placid](../../../traits/instructions/placid.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve staying calm and tolerant under irritation, but patient centers on accepting delays and giving others time, while placid centers on temperament, being slow to anger and answering evenly; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe staying calm and unbothered by delays and irritations; placid stresses an even temper that is slow to anger, while patient stresses tolerance of waiting, so they differ only in emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means staying calm and tolerant when things drag on or irritate, accepting delays without frustration and giving others the time they need without complaint.
- **patriarchal** (`patriarchal#1`, cut-off 3) by [antifeminist](../../../traits/instructions/antifeminist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both hold that men should lead and women should defer, but antifeminist adds active opposition to women's causes and scoffing at sexism, while patriarchal is the belief in male authority itself."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on the belief that men should lead over women; antifeminist adds active opposition to women's causes and dismissal of sexism, a difference in emphasis rather than concept.")
  Gloss: This means believing that men should hold authority over women in family, work and public life, and that this arrangement is natural and right.
- **patrician** (`patrician#1`, cut-off 3) by [old money](../../../traits/instructions/old_money.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe upper-class standing, but 'old money' specifically means inherited, multigenerational wealth and its trappings, while 'patrician' means aristocratic rank or bearing, which need not involve wealth."), Opus 3 ("Old money is essentially patrician upper-class standing, with added emphasis on wealth and trappings inherited across generations.")
  Gloss: This means being of aristocratic, upper-class social standing.
- **pedagogical** (`pedagogical#1`, cut-off 3) by [didactic](../../../traits/instructions/didactic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve treating exchanges as lessons and explaining fully, but pedagogical stresses clear step-by-step teaching while didactic stresses lecturing and not letting others work things out, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe treating exchanges as lessons with full explanations; didactic is the same teaching stance carried further, toward lecturing rather than letting people work things out.")
  Gloss: This means teaching in a didactic manner, laying out concepts step by step, explaining the reasons behind each point, and treating every exchange as a lesson to be taught clearly.
- **penurious** (`penurious#1`, cut-off 3) by [frugal](../../../traits/instructions/frugal.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve minimal spending, but penurious is excessive, grudging stinginess even when spending is needed, while frugal is prudent, sensible economy; they share a core but differ in degree and evaluative stance."), Opus 3 ("Both are about minimizing spending, but penurious is a grudging, excessive refusal even of needed spending, while frugal is sensible economy that still buys what is needed, so penurious is the same quality carried further.")
  Gloss: This means counting every coin and grudging each expense, refusing to spend money even when spending would be reasonable, generous, or plainly needed.
- **peppy** (`peppy#1`, cut-off 3) by [energetic](../../../traits/instructions/energetic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe high, brisk energy, but peppy emphasizes bright, enthusiastic spirit in interactions while energetic emphasizes stamina and sustained activity, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe high, brisk energy: peppy stresses bright, enthusiastic spirit, while energetic stresses tireless get-up-and-go.")
  Gloss: This means bringing a bright, quick, high-spirited energy to every exchange, meeting ideas and people with visible enthusiasm and an eagerness to get moving.
- **perceptive** (`perceptive#1`, cut-off 3) by [observant](../../../traits/instructions/observant.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve keen noticing, but perceptive adds understanding and insight while observant is about spotting details in the surroundings; each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Observant covers the keen-noticing half of perceptive, while perceptive also takes in understanding, so the difference is one of scope.")
  Gloss: This means noticing and understanding things readily and keenly.
- **percipient** (`percipient#1`, cut-off 3) by [socially-perceptive](../../../traits/instructions/socially_perceptive.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve quickly noticing subtle cues, but percipient is general (any situation, plus voicing it) while socially-perceptive is limited to social and emotional cues, so they share a core with each adding something."), Opus 3 ("Socially-perceptive is percipience narrowed to social cues and mood, without the emphasis on speaking up, so it is the same concept in a narrower scope.")
  Gloss: This means noticing subtle details and grasping what is happening in a situation quickly, often before others have registered it, and saying so when one sees it.
- **perspicacious** (`perspicacious#1`, cut-off 3) by [socially-perceptive](../../../traits/instructions/socially_perceptive.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve sharp noticing of what others miss, but perspicacious is broader insight into situations, motives and details, while socially-perceptive is limited to reading social cues and mood."), Opus 3 ("Social perceptiveness is perspicacity narrowed to social cues and moods, while perspicacity also covers seeing through to hidden motives and to details in general.")
  Gloss: This means noticing what others overlook, reading situations and people with sharp insight, and seeing through appearances to the hidden motives or details beneath them.
- **perturbable** (`perturbable#1`, cut-off 3) by [fragile](../../../traits/instructions/fragile.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe being easily thrown off by disruption and slow to recover, but perturbable centers on emotional rattling by small upsets while fragile centers on brittleness under criticism, setbacks and pressure, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe being easily thrown off balance emotionally and slow to recover; fragile shifts the emphasis to brittleness under adversity and pressure rather than upset at small disruptions.")
  Gloss: This means being easily upset, unsettled or rattled emotionally, so that small disruptions or unexpected news quickly throw one off balance and take a long time to settle again.
- **pettish** (`pettish#1`, cut-off 3) by [sulky](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve sulking after slights and lingering resentment, but pettish adds childish fretting and peevishness over small things while sulky stresses quiet withdrawal, so each has features the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe sulking and lingering resentment after slights; pettish adds a childish, peevish fretfulness over small things, which is a shift in emphasis rather than a different concept.")
  Gloss: This means being quick to sulk and fret over small slights, sulking in a childish way when things do not go one's own way and carrying a peevish mood for some time afterward.
- **phenomenal** (`phenomenal#1`, cut-off 3) by [competent](../../../traits/instructions/competent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe skill at one's work, but phenomenal means exceptional, standout excellence while competent means reliably adequate, so they differ in degree and the other is not simply a milder version of the same thing."), Opus 3 ("Both describe skill at one's work, but phenomenal is exceptional excellence while competent is solid adequacy, so they differ in degree.")
  Gloss: This means doing one's work at an exceptionally high standard, performing with remarkable skill that sets one apart from most others in the same field.
- **philistine** (`philistine#1`, cut-off 3) by [conventional (HEXACO)](../../../traits/instructions/conventional_hexaco.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve indifference to art and culture, but philistine adds active scorn and hostility toward those who value it, while conventional is mild incuriosity and a lack of pull toward unconventional ideas."), Opus 3 ("Both describe low engagement with art and ideas, but conventional is passive indifference while philistine adds active scorn and hostility toward culture and its lovers, so philistine is the same lack carried further.")
  Gloss: This means dismissing art, learning and culture as pointless or even suspect, and treating anyone who loves them with impatience, scorn or open hostility.
- **philomath** (`philomath#1`, cut-off 3) by [curious](../../../traits/instructions/curious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a love of learning and interest in new subjects, but philomath stresses wide reading and in-depth study, while curious stresses interest, questions and wonder, so neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Both are a genuine love of learning new things, and philomath is that curiosity carried further into sustained, wide-ranging, in-depth study.")
  Gloss: This means pursuing learning and knowledge for their own sake, reading widely and treating every new subject as something worth studying in depth.
- **phoenix** (`phoenix#1`, cut-off 3) by [resilient](../../../traits/instructions/resilient.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both are about recovering from setbacks and carrying on, but 'phoenix' stresses rising again and starting over after total collapse, while 'resilient' is broader, adding quick adaptation and emotional stability during adversity."), Opus 3 ("Phoenix is resilience at its extreme: recovering and starting over after total ruin, rather than recovering from ordinary setbacks.")
  Gloss: This means getting back up after ruin, collapse or defeat and starting over again, every time, without treating the fall as the end of one's story.
- **pigeon-hearted** (`pigeon_hearted#1`, cut-off 3) by [cowardly](../../../traits/instructions/cowardly.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe timidity and shrinking from danger or confrontation, but pigeon-hearted adds easy startling and losing nerve, while cowardly adds leaving others to face the danger, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe fear overriding courage and shrinking from confrontation; cowardly stresses the moral failure of abandoning others when it matters, while pigeon-hearted stresses jumpy timidity.")
  Gloss: This means startling easily at small threats, shrinking from confrontation, and losing one's nerve whenever a situation calls for boldness or resolve.
- **pillar** (`pillar#1`, cut-off 3) by [dependable](../../../traits/instructions/dependable.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve being reliable and counted on, but 'pillar' adds being a central mainstay supporting a community or institution, while 'dependable' is general follow-through on commitments."), Opus 3 ("A pillar is essentially dependability applied to holding up a community or institution, a narrower and stronger form of being someone others can count on.")
  Gloss: This means being a dependable mainstay who keeps supporting one's community or institution through steady effort, showing up reliably when others need someone to hold things up.
- **pin-headed** (`pin_headed#1`, cut-off 3) by [slow-witted](../../../traits/instructions/slow_witted.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe poor mental sharpness, but pin-headed stresses foolish, poor reasoning and missing the obvious, while slow-witted stresses slowness in grasping and replying; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe low intelligence, but slow-witted stresses slowness in grasping things while pin-headed stresses foolish reasoning, so they differ mainly in emphasis.")
  Gloss: This means reasoning poorly and missing what is obvious, being foolish and dim-witted in one's thinking as a settled trait.
- **pious** (`pious#1`, cut-off 3) by [religious](../../../traits/instructions/religious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve faith in God, but pious stresses sincere devotion and a life built around prayer and worship, while religious here stresses using scripture and divine authority in reasoning and decisions, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both center on faith, with piety being a deeper, practice-centered devotion that largely entails the faith-based reasoning described as religious, while religious emphasizes the intellectual framing.")
  Gloss: This means living by a deep and sincere devotion to God, structuring one's days around prayer, worship and obedience to sacred teaching, and treating faith as the center of one's character.
- **placable** (`placable#1`, cut-off 3) by [agreeable (HEXACO)](../../../traits/instructions/agreeable_hexaco.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve forgiveness and not holding grudges, but agreeable (HEXACO) also covers lenient judgment, cooperation and temper control, while placable is specifically about being readily soothed after an offence."), Opus 3 ("HEXACO agreeableness contains forgiveness and keeping one's temper, which is placability, and adds lenient judgement and willingness to compromise, so it is a broader version of the same core concept.")
  Gloss: This means letting anger drain away quickly once an offence is acknowledged, and holding no grudge against those who have wronged one, so that one is readily soothed and forgiving.
- **planned** (`planned#1`, cut-off 3) by [methodical](../../../traits/instructions/methodical.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve working from a plan, but 'planned' stresses thinking through steps beforehand, while 'methodical' adds step-by-step execution and sticking to the plan; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Methodical working from a plan in ordered steps entails being planned, adding an emphasis on sequential execution and sticking to the plan.")
  Gloss: This means acting with deliberate organization, thinking through steps before taking them.
- **planning ahead** (`planning_ahead#1`, cut-off 3) by [prudent](../../../traits/instructions/prudent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve weighing consequences and saving for later needs, but planning ahead centers on forethought and future-oriented allocation, while prudence centers on risk awareness and caution about costly mistakes."), Opus 3 ("Both describe foresight that weighs consequences and saves for future needs, with prudence leaning more toward risk-avoidance and the cost of mistakes.")
  Gloss: This means weighing consequences before acting, setting money, time and effort aside for later needs, and choosing the course that serves one's future self over immediate comfort.
- **plays fair** (`plays_fair#1`, cut-off 4) by [fair](../../../traits/instructions/fair.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe even-handed treatment under the same rules and refusing unfair advantage; 'fair' adds hearing each side and no favorites, while 'plays fair' stresses honesty, but they are nearly the same concept."), Opus 4 ("Both describe even-handed dealing under the same rules with no cheating for advantage; they are essentially interchangeable.")
  Gloss: This means keeping one's dealings with others honest and even-handed, giving everyone the same rules and the same chance, and refusing to bend the truth or the terms to gain an advantage.
- **pliant** (`pliant#1`, cut-off 4) by [malleable](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe readily yielding to others' pressure and dropping one's own position; malleable adds shifting loyalties and opinions to match the forceful speaker, but the core is essentially the same."), Opus 4 ("Both describe readily yielding one's position under pressure from others; malleable extends this slightly to plans and loyalties, but it is essentially the same concept.")
  Gloss: This means giving way readily when others press their wishes, and dropping one's own position as soon as someone else pushes back on it.
- **polarized** (`polarized#1`, cut-off 3) by [extremist](../../../traits/instructions/extremist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve extreme positions and rejecting middle ground, but polarized stresses a two-camp framing while extremist stresses far-edge views, hostility to compromise and total victory, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe holding views at the extremes and rejecting middle ground; extremist pushes this further into scorn for compromise and a demand for total victory.")

- **politic** (`politic#1`, cut-off 3) by [prudent](../../../traits/instructions/prudent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve cautious weighing of consequences, but 'politic' centers on tactful speech and conduct while 'prudent' centers on risk-awareness and financial/planning caution, so they share a core but each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Politic is essentially prudence applied to one's words and social conduct, so it is a narrower-scope form of the same careful, consequence-weighing judgment.")

- **politically liberal** (`politically_liberal#1`, cut-off 3) by [progressive](../../../traits/instructions/progressive.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both favor reform over tradition, but 'politically liberal' names a specific set of social and economic positions while 'progressive' is a broader orientation toward change that need not be political or tied to those policies."), Opus 3 ("Political liberalism as described is a specific political form of the broader change-favoring, anti-traditional stance that progressive describes, so they are the same concept differing in scope.")

- **post-modern** (`post_modern#1`, cut-off 3) by [relativist](../../../traits/instructions/relativist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both reject universal, final truths and treat accounts as perspective-dependent, but post-modern stresses doubting grand narratives while relativist stresses truth and morality depending on context, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both reject a single objective truth and treat accounts as perspective-bound; relativism states the same stance more absolutely and extends it explicitly to morality.")

- **practically wise** (`practically_wise#1`, cut-off 3) by [wise](../../../traits/instructions/wise.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve sound judgment, but practical wisdom focuses on workable everyday decisions over theory, while wisdom is broader, covering foresight, learning from experience, and lasting advice; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe sound judgment about what matters and how choices play out; practical wisdom is a narrower, everyday-focused form of general wisdom.")

- **practiced** (`practiced#1`, cut-off 3) by [competent](../../../traits/instructions/competent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe handling work with a sure hand, but 'practiced' stresses skill built through years of repetition and ease, while 'competent' stresses adequate, reliable results without implying long experience."), Opus 3 ("Both mean handling work with sure, capable hands; practiced is competence carried further, earned through long repetition until it is effortless.")

- **prating** (`prating#1`, cut-off 3) by [chattering](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe incessant idle talk, but prating stresses foolish, senseless, time-wasting content while chattering stresses a quick, continuous stream that fills silences, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe incessant talk of little substance; prating stresses its foolishness and time-wasting, while chattering stresses the quick, pause-filling flow.")

- **preferent** (`preferent#1`, cut-off 3) by [cliquish](../../../traits/instructions/cliquish.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve favoring some people over others, but cliquish is specifically in-group loyalty with exclusion of outsiders, while preferent is general favoritism not tied to a circle or to exclusion."), Opus 3 ("Cliquishness is a narrower form of favoritism, favoring one's own circle and excluding outsiders, so it implies preferential treatment but adds group exclusivity.")

- **prejudicious** (`prejudicious#1`, cut-off 3) by [ageist](../../../traits/instructions/ageist.json): Sonnet 2 ("Ageism is a specific kind of prejudgment based on age, so it falls under the broader prejudicial habit of judging people by category before knowing them, but the target is general and ageist is narrower and adds a readiness to say so."), Opus 3 ("Ageism is prejudgment narrowed to the single axis of age, so it is the same concept as being prejudicious with a narrower scope.")

- **princely** (`princely#1`, cut-off 3) by [generous](../../../traits/instructions/generous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve giving freely to others, but princely adds noble bearing and lavish, grand-scale generosity, while generous covers any kind of giving, including sacrificial giving, without the regal manner."), Opus 3 ("Princely includes lavish generosity plus a noble bearing, so it is essentially generosity carried further with an added aristocratic style.")

- **private** (`private#1`, cut-off 3) by [reserved](../../../traits/instructions/reserved.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve withholding personal feelings and keeping quiet reserve, but 'private' centers on guarding personal history and circumstances while 'reserved' centers on emotional restraint and polite distance, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe withholding one's personal feelings and matters from others; reserved carries the same reticence a bit further, adding an outward polite distance.")

- **prompt** (`prompt#1`, cut-off 3) by [hurried](../../../traits/instructions/hurried.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve acting at once without delay, but 'prompt' is about responsive, timely action on requests, while 'hurried' adds a sense of urgency and rush about everything, even when inconvenient; they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe acting at once without delay; hurried carries this further into treating everything as urgent regardless of inconvenience.")

- **prompt and efficient** (`prompt_and_efficient#1`, cut-off 3) by [efficient](../../../traits/instructions/efficient.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve getting tasks done quickly without waste, but 'prompt and efficient' stresses speed and no delay, while 'efficient' stresses minimal effort and avoiding redundancy, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both are about getting tasks done quickly without wasted steps. - **prone to absorption** (`prone_to_absorption#1`, cut-off 3) by [focused](../../../traits/instructions/focused.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve sustained attention on a task through to completion, but absorption is being engrossed so the world fades, while focus is deliberately resisting distractions; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe sustained attention on a task until it is finished; absorption is a deeper, more involuntary version of the same focus.")

- **prone to worry** (`prone_to_worry#1`, cut-off 3) by [neurotic (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/neurotic_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("Neuroticism includes fretting over what could go wrong, which is the core of proneness to worry, but it also covers irritability, sadness, self-consciousness, impulsivity and stress vulnerability, so it is a much broader trait."), Opus 3 ("Neuroticism includes worry as one facet and adds anger, sadness, self-consciousness, impulsiveness and vulnerability, so it is a broader version of the same core.")

- **purposed** (`purposed#1`, cut-off 3) by [persevering](../../../traits/instructions/persevering.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve steadfast pursuit of a goal despite obstacles, but 'purposed' stresses a fixed aim and not drifting, while 'persevering' stresses enduring failure and restarting until done; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both mean holding to a chosen goal despite obstacles. - **reclusive** (`reclusive#1`, cut-off 3) by [solitary](../../../traits/instructions/solitary.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe keeping apart from others, but 'solitary' is a calm preference for being alone, while 'reclusive' stresses withdrawing from society and avoiding contact, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe keeping away from others by preference, with reclusive being a more extreme, society-wide withdrawal.")

- **religiously devout** (`religiously_devout#1`, cut-off 3) by [religious](../../../traits/instructions/religious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern religious faith shaping a person's life, but devout stresses sincere commitment and daily practice, while religious as described stresses reasoning from scripture and divine authority; each can occur without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe faith guiding one's judgments and decisions. - **relishes risky careers** (`relishes_risky_careers#1`, cut-off 3) by [risk-seeking](../../../traits/instructions/risk_seeking.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve embracing risk and uncertainty, but the target is specifically about enjoying dangerous careers while the other is a general disposition to gamble for bigger payoffs, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Relishing risky careers is risk-seeking narrowed to the domain of work, with added enjoyment of danger; general risk-seeking covers any gamble.")

- **resents having to wait** (`resents_having_to_wait#1`, cut-off 3) by [aggrieved](../../../traits/instructions/aggrieved.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve feeling wronged and nursing a grievance, but the target is specifically about resentment at being kept waiting, while aggrieved is a general tendency to feel wronged across many situations."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on feeling personally wronged and holding the grievance, but one is tied to delays while the other is a general disposition, so this is a narrow case within the broader trait.")

- **respects human dignity** (`respects_human_dignity#1`, cut-off 3) by [humanistic](../../../traits/instructions/humanistic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Humanistic is a broader trait that includes respecting human dignity along with cultural sensitivity, social awareness and concern for community well-being, so the target is one component of it."), Opus 3 ("Humanistic explicitly includes respecting human dignity and adds cultural sensitivity, social implications and group effects, so it is a broader concept with the target at its core.")

- **rule bound** (`rule_bound#1`, cut-off 4) by [rule-abiding](../../../traits/instructions/rule_abiding.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both describe following rules strictly without deviation; the other adds legal compliance and asking permission, but the core is the same, with slightly broader scope."), Opus 4 ("Both describe strict adherence to rules without deviation. - **secularizing** (`secularizing#1`, cut-off 3) by [secular](../../../traits/instructions/secular.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern religion playing a small role in a person's outlook, but 'secularizing' describes a gradual process of drifting away from faith, while 'secular' describes a stable non-religious, evidence-based way of thinking, so neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Secularizing is the process of moving toward the secular state, and secular is that state already reached; they are the same concept differing in emphasis on process versus endpoint.")

- **self-loving** (`self_loving#1`, cut-off 3) by [grandiose](../../../traits/instructions/grandiose.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve an inflated view of one's own worth, but grandiose stresses exaggerated claims of superiority and exceptional abilities, while self-loving stresses vanity, self-admiration and expecting others to share one's regard."), Opus 3 ("Both describe an inflated sense of one's own worth.   Gloss: This means refusing offers of help and turning down support even when one plainly needs it, treating any reliance on others as weakness and insisting on handling everything alone.
- **semitransparent** (`semitransparent#1`, cut-off 3) by [opaque](../../../traits/instructions/opaque.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern how much of one's inner life is disclosed; semitransparent is partial disclosure while opaque is near-total withholding, so they lie at neighbouring points on the same dimension, differing in degree."), Opus 3 ("Both describe deliberately withholding parts of oneself from others; opaque is the same withholding carried much further, with only the strictly necessary shared, and it focuses on reasoning and information rather than feelings.")
  Gloss: This means letting others see only part of one's inner life, sharing some feelings and facts while keeping the rest deliberately out of view.
- **senile** (`senile#1`, cut-off 3) by [forgetful](../../../traits/instructions/forgetful.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve losing names, dates and repeating questions, but senile is age-related mental decline including confusion, while forgetful is just memory lapses of any cause, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Senile is forgetfulness carried further, adding general confusion and an old-age cause, while forgetful brings nothing senile lacks.")
  Gloss: This means being mentally confused and forgetful from old age, losing track of names, dates and recent events and repeating oneself.
- **sensation-seeking** (`sensation_seeking#1`, cut-off 3) by [adventurous](../../../traits/instructions/adventurous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve seeking novelty and thrill and disliking routine, but sensation-seeking stresses risk and intense experiences while adventurous stresses openness to the unfamiliar, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe seeking novelty and thrills and chafing at routine; sensation-seeking just puts more weight on intensity and risk.")

- **sentimental about belongings** (`sentimental_about_belongings#1`, cut-off 3) by [sentimental](../../../traits/instructions/sentimental.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve emotional attachment to memories and keepsakes, but the other is broader (tearing up, letting fondness sway choices), while the target is specifically about difficulty parting with possessions."), Opus 3 ("Both describe emotional attachment rooted in memories, but the target confines it to possessions while the other is a broader sentimentality that includes keepsakes along with tearful goodbyes and fondness for people and places, so they differ only in scope.")

- **serviceable** (`serviceable#1`, cut-off 3) by [competent](../../../traits/instructions/competent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern work that gets the job done reliably, but serviceable stresses adequate, dependable output while competent stresses skill and knowing how to do it right; neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe turning out sound work that gets the job done. - **severe** (`severe#1`, cut-off 3) by [strict](../../../traits/instructions/strict.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve holding people to high standards without leniency, but severe adds a stern, unsmiling manner and harsh judgment, while strict stresses demanding results and a belief in growth through pushing."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on holding people to strict standards without leniency. - **sexless** (`sexless#1`, cut-off 3) by [chaste](../../../traits/instructions/chaste.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve absence of sexual desire, but chaste adds purity, moral restraint and avoidance of sensual topics, while sexless is simply lacking desire as a settled condition."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on being untouched by sexual desire; chaste, as described, extends that absence into pure speech and turning away from sensual topics.")
  Gloss: This means lacking any sexual desire or interest, and feeling no pull toward sexual activity as a settled part of one's life.
- **sheep-headed** (`sheep_headed#1`, cut-off 3) by [slow-witted](../../../traits/instructions/slow_witted.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve being slow to grasp things, but sheep-headed adds thoughtless, foolish acting in everyday dealings, while slow-witted is only about slow comprehension and delayed replies."), Opus 3 ("Both describe slowness of understanding, but sheep-headed also includes thoughtless action and visible foolishness, while slow-witted is narrower and covers only slow comprehension.")
  Gloss: This means being slow to grasp things and often acting without thinking, so that one's foolishness shows in plain, ordinary dealings with others.
- **shifting identity** (`shifting_identity#1`, cut-off 3) by [self-uncertain](../../../traits/instructions/self_uncertain.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe an unstable or unsettled sense of self, but 'shifting identity' stresses moment-to-moment change while 'self-uncertain' stresses not knowing who one is or what one values, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe an unsettled, unstable sense of self; shifting identity stresses moment-to-moment change, while self-uncertain stresses not knowing who one is, which also shows up as shifting self-descriptions.")

- **siding** (`siding#1`, cut-off 3) by [partisan](../../../traits/instructions/partisan.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve backing one side over another instead of staying neutral, but siding is a general act of taking a side in any dispute, while partisan is a habitual, political, line-toeing, bad-faith-assuming stance, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Partisanship is siding made habitual and extreme, applied to political controversy with no pretense of balance. - **silk-stocking** (`silk_stocking#1`, cut-off 3) by [wealthy](../../../traits/instructions/wealthy.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern being rich, but 'silk-stocking' stresses membership of the upper class (social standing), while 'wealthy' stresses material affluence; each can exist without the other."), Opus 3 ("Silk-stocking is wealth plus upper-class social standing, a narrower version of being wealthy.")

- **silly** (`silly#1`, cut-off 3) by [foolish](../../../traits/instructions/foolish.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern poor judgment and unwise choices, but silly stresses careless speech and acting without weighing consequences, while foolish stresses missing what matters, not learning from experience, and giving bad advice; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe a persistent lack of good judgment in choices and consequences, and foolish only shifts the emphasis toward failing to learn and giving bad advice.")

- **simple-hearted** (`simple_hearted#1`, cut-off 3) by [trusting](../../../traits/instructions/trusting.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve expecting good faith and taking people at their word, but simple-hearted also includes lacking cunning or hidden calculation in one's own dealings, which trusting does not imply."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on taking people at their word and expecting good faith, but simple-hearted also covers having no cunning or calculation of one's own, so it is somewhat broader.")

- **single-mindedly** (`single_mindedly#1`, cut-off 3) by [focused](../../../traits/instructions/focused.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve resisting distraction, but single-mindedly is sustained devotion to one overarching goal that excludes side interests, while focused is task-level attention and finishing things one at a time, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both mean keeping attention undiverted, but single-mindedness carries it further, subordinating all effort and interests to one overarching goal rather than one task at a time.")

- **skimpy** (`skimpy#1`, cut-off 3) by [frugal](../../../traits/instructions/frugal.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve spending as little as possible, but skimpy adds stinginess in giving and begrudging others, while frugal is prudent, need-based economy without that meanness."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on spending as little as possible; skimpy carries this further into begrudging stinginess toward others, while frugal is the plainer thrift.")

- **slangy** (`slangy#1`, cut-off 3) by [casual](../../../traits/instructions/casual.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve informal, conversational language, but slangy specifically stresses slang and clipped colloquialisms, while casual is a broader relaxed tone that can exist without slang."), Opus 3 ("Both describe informal, conversational language, and slangy is a more extreme form of casual speech that leans on slang.")
  Gloss: This means speaking and writing in casual slang, favoring informal words, clipped phrasing and colloquial expressions over formal or standard wording.
- **slashing** (`slashing#1`, cut-off 3) by [harsh](../../../traits/instructions/harsh.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve delivering wounding, unsoftened criticism, but 'harsh' is broader (severity, quick judgment, heavy-handedness) while 'slashing' is specifically a scathing, cutting speaking style."), Opus 3 ("Both involve cutting, unsoftened criticism. Harsh is broader, taking in general severity, heavy-handedness and quickness to judge, while slashing is specifically a scathingly sharp way of speaking.")
  Gloss: This means speaking with a cutting, scathingly sharp edge, delivering criticism and remarks in a manner that wounds rather than softens.
- **slogger** (`slogger#1`, cut-off 3) by [persevering](../../../traits/instructions/persevering.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve sticking with a task until it is finished despite boredom, but the slogger is about steady plodding through tedious repetitive work, while persevering is about persisting toward a hard goal through failure and rejection."), Opus 3 ("Both describe sticking with a task until it is done, with slogging as the narrower case of perseverance applied to tedious, repetitive work rather than to failure and rejection.")
  Gloss: This means grinding steadily through tedious, repetitive work without complaint or shortcuts, plodding on long after the task has lost any appeal and staying with it until it is finished.
- **slow to forgive** (`slow_to_forgive#1`, cut-off 3) by [quarrelsome (HEXACO)](../../../traits/instructions/quarrelsome_hexaco.json): Sonnet 2 ("Quarrelsome as described includes grudge-holding, which overlaps with slow to forgive, but it also covers criticalness, stubbornness in argument and quick anger, which the target lacks."), Opus 3 ("Quarrelsome includes nursing grudges, which is the target's core, but widens it to criticalness, stubbornness in arguments and quick anger, so it is a broader version of the same unforgiving stance.")

- **smutty** (`smutty#1`, cut-off 3) by [obscene](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve crude sexual talk and innuendo, but smutty stresses habitually steering talk toward bawdy jokes and double meanings, while obscene stresses offensive, shocking lewdness, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe crude sexual talk and innuendo; obscene stresses offensive, shocking lewdness, a stronger degree of the same quality, while smutty stresses steering conversation toward sex.")
  Gloss: This means turning ordinary talk toward sex, reaching for crude innuendo and bawdy jokes at every opening, and finding double meanings in whatever anyone says.
- **socially at ease** (`socially_at_ease#1`, cut-off 3) by [unselfconscious](../../../traits/instructions/unselfconscious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve ease around others without self-consciousness, but 'socially at ease' is broader (relaxed, confident with anyone) while 'unselfconscious' focuses specifically on not being aware of being watched; each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe moving among people without self-consciousness. Unselfconscious narrows this to obliviousness to being watched and carries it further, while socially at ease covers broader relaxed confidence.")
  Gloss: This means staying relaxed and confident in conversation with strangers and friends alike, moving among other people without strain, self-consciousness, or a need to perform.
- **softish** (`softish#1`, cut-off 3) by [lenient](../../../traits/instructions/lenient.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve going easy on others and avoiding strict discipline; 'softish' adds soft-heartedness, quick forgiveness and self-leniency, while 'lenient' adds a low bar and a comfort-over-pushing belief, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe going easy on people rather than imposing strict discipline. Softish is a milder version that adds soft-heartedness and leniency toward oneself, while lenient adds a deliberate stance of keeping the bar low.")
  Gloss: This means being mildly soft-hearted and lenient, quick to forgive small lapses and slow to impose strict discipline on others or on oneself.
- **sottish** (`sottish#1`, cut-off 3) by [heavy-drinker](../../../traits/instructions/heavy_drinker.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe habitual excessive drinking, but sottish adds a stupor with dulled wits and conduct, while heavy-drinker only stresses quantity and frequency, so neither fully implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe habitual excessive drinking; sottish carries it further, to stupor and dulled wits, while heavy-drinker is a milder degree of the same habit.")

- **sound** (`sound#1`, cut-off 3) by [wise](../../../traits/instructions/wise.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve good judgment and reliable advice, but 'wise' adds foresight and experience-based insight while 'sound' stresses steady, clear-headed reliability, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe good judgment and advice that holds up; wise carries it further with deeper insight, foresight and learning from experience, and it largely implies soundness.")

- **speedy** (`speedy#1`, cut-off 3) by [hurried](../../../traits/instructions/hurried.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve acting immediately without delay, but speedy is efficient prompt turnaround while hurried adds a pressured, treat-everything-as-urgent quality; each can occur without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe dealing with things immediately; hurried is speedy carried further, into treating everything as urgent however inconvenient.")

- **spiritual-minded** (`spiritual_minded#1`, cut-off 3) by [religious](../../../traits/instructions/religious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a faith-based lens on life, but spiritual-minded centers on meaning and the sacred in a broad, possibly non-institutional way, while religious stresses scripture, divine authority and tradition as grounds for reasoning; each can exist without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe understanding the world through a spiritual or sacred lens; 'religious' is a narrower version anchored in scripture, theology and tradition.")

- **splitting the difference** (`splitting_the_difference#1`, cut-off 3) by [moderate](../../../traits/instructions/moderate.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both center on seeking compromise and middle ground, but splitting the difference is a specific mechanical negotiating habit of taking the midpoint, while moderate is a broader disposition against extremes and polarizing stances."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on seeking the middle ground and compromise. - **standoffish** (`standoffish#1`, cut-off 3) by [reserved](../../../traits/instructions/reserved.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve emotional distance and withholding personal disclosure, but standoffish adds aloofness and unwelcoming coolness, while reserved is a more neutral, polite restraint."), Opus 3 ("Both describe keeping distance and withholding personal disclosure, but standoffish carries reserve further into a cool aloofness that makes approach feel unwelcome.")

- **stellar** (`stellar#1`, cut-off 3) by [competent](../../../traits/instructions/competent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both concern work quality, but stellar means outstanding, excellent performance while competent means reliably adequate, capable work; this is the same quality at different degrees."), Opus 3 ("Both describe quality of work performance, but stellar is outstanding excellence while competent is solid adequacy, so stellar is the same concept carried much further.")

- **stern** (`stern#1`, cut-off 3) by [strict](../../../traits/instructions/strict.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve holding others to demanding standards without softness, but stern also includes a severe, unsmiling demeanor while strict emphasizes demanding results and pushing people to grow, so they share a core with different additions."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on holding others to exacting standards without softening; stern adds a severe, unsmiling demeanour, so it differs mainly in emphasis.")

- **stoical** (`stoical#1`, cut-off 3) by [rugged](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve enduring hardship without complaint, but stoical stresses calm composure and no visible distress, while rugged stresses self-reliant resilience and handling problems alone."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on enduring hardship without complaint; rugged mainly adds an emphasis on self-reliance and handling problems alone.")

- **storied** (`storied#1`, cut-off 3) by [famous](../../../traits/instructions/famous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve being widely known, but 'storied' stresses a legendary reputation built on tales, while 'famous' stresses public recognition and visibility; neither implies the other."), Opus 3 ("Storied is fame carried further into legend, a celebrated reputation with tales attached, while famous is simply being widely known and recognized.")

- **stouthearted** (`stouthearted#1`, cut-off 3) by [brave](../../../traits/instructions/brave.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve facing fear and danger with resolve, but stouthearted stresses steady endurance through hardship while brave stresses acting despite fear to confront a threat, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe courage in the face of fear; stouthearted stresses steady endurance through hardship, while brave stresses actively confronting danger.")

- **strenuous** (`strenuous#1`, cut-off 3) by [industrious](../../../traits/instructions/industrious.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve working hard, but strenuous stresses intense vigor and effort in each task, while industrious stresses habitual diligence, persistence and dislike of idleness, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe working hard as a matter of course: strenuous stresses the vigor and intensity of the effort, industrious its steady, habitual diligence.")

- **structureless** (`structureless#1`, cut-off 3) by [stream-of-consciousness](../../../traits/instructions/stream_of_consciousness.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe thought that wanders from idea to idea without imposed order; structureless also covers haphazard handling of tasks and conduct, while stream-of-consciousness centres on spontaneous associative thinking."), Opus 3 ("Both describe an unorganized flow of thought, but structureless is broader, also covering haphazard task handling, while stream-of-consciousness centres on associative thinking.")

- **stuffy** (`stuffy#1`, cut-off 3) by [formal](../../../traits/instructions/formal.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve formal, non-casual manner, but stuffy adds rigid conventionality and discomfort with relaxed behavior across all dealings, while formal is just a proper, dignified register of language suited to the context."), Opus 3 ("Stuffy is formality carried to an extreme: rigid, applied in every setting, and uneasy with casualness, whereas formal is a professional register suited to the context.")

- **sublime** (`sublime#1`, cut-off 3) by [dignified](../../../traits/instructions/dignified.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a poised, dignified bearing, but 'sublime' stresses lofty, elevated excellence in every gesture while 'dignified' stresses self-respect, composure, and avoiding ridicule, so they share a core and each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Sublime is dignified bearing carried further, to a lofty, elevated excellence beyond ordinary poise and composure.")

- **substantive** (`substantive#1`, cut-off 3) by [thorough](../../../traits/instructions/thorough.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both stress depth over surface-level answers, but substantive is about real content versus filler, while thorough adds comprehensiveness across dimensions and edge cases; each can occur without the other."), Opus 3 ("Both reject surface-level answers in favour of real depth. - **sucker** (`sucker#1`, cut-off 3) by [credulous](../../../traits/instructions/credulous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve readily believing what one is told, but 'sucker' adds being repeatedly exploited and failing to learn, while 'credulous' is only the disposition to believe without evidence."), Opus 3 ("Both are uncritical belief in what one is told; sucker adds the outcome of being repeatedly exploited, so it is a more consequential version of credulity.")

- **surprising** (`surprising#1`, cut-off 3) by [spontaneous](../../../traits/instructions/spontaneous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both center on unpredictability and avoiding the expected, but 'surprising' stresses deliberately choosing unforeseen moves while the other stresses variety and avoiding formulaic patterns, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe unpredictability and avoiding set patterns. Surprising stresses habitually confounding observers' expectations, while spontaneous stresses variety and non-formulaic approach, so they share a core but differ in emphasis.")

- **swift** (`swift#1`, cut-off 3) by [hurried](../../../traits/instructions/hurried.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve acting immediately without delay, but 'swift' is efficient promptness while 'hurried' adds a pressured sense that everything is urgent, so each carries something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe dealing with things at once without delay. Hurried adds treating everything as urgent and rushing regardless of convenience, which makes it a more extreme, pressured version of the same promptness.")

- **swinish** (`swinish#1`, cut-off 3) by [crude](../../../seed_queue.json) (seed queue, candidate): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve coarse, unrefined behavior and speech with no regard for polish, but swinish adds greedy eating and brutish disregard for others' feelings, while crude focuses on vulgar language and humor."), Opus 3 ("Both describe coarse, unrefined vulgarity. - **tactfully clarifying** (`tactfully_clarifying#1`, cut-off 3) by [tactful](../../../traits/instructions/tactful.json): Sonnet 2 ("Tactful is the general trait of choosing sensitive wording; tactfully clarifying applies that specifically to making unclear points plain or correcting matters, so the target is a narrower subset with an added clarifying function."), Opus 3 ("Tactfully clarifying is tactfulness applied specifically to clarifying or correcting, so it is a narrower scope of the same sensitivity in wording.")

- **tactless** (`tactless#1`, cut-off 3) by [blunt](../../../traits/instructions/blunt.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve direct speech without cushioning, but tactless adds disregard for others' feelings while blunt is about honest directness and may be deliberate and considerate."), Opus 3 ("Tactless is bluntness carried further, adding disregard for how the words land, while bluntness itself is simply direct, unsoftened delivery.")

- **takes things lightly** (`takes_things_lightly#1`, cut-off 3) by [emotionally-stable (Big Five)](../../../traits/instructions/emotionally_stable_big_five.json): Sonnet 2 ("They share a core of staying calm and shrugging off setbacks, but emotional stability is much broader (slow to anger, at ease among strangers, resisting temptation, steady under stress), while taking things lightly is specifically about not dwelling on worries."), Opus 3 ("Taking things lightly, staying relaxed and not dwelling on worries or setbacks, is essentially the low-anxiety core of emotional stability, which is the broader version adding even temper, social ease and self-control.")

- **tart** (`tart#1`, cut-off 3) by [harsh](../../../traits/instructions/harsh.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve cutting, wounding speech, but harsh is broader (severity, quick judgment, unsoftened truths) while tart is specifically a caustic, sharp-tongued style of remark."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on cutting, wounding remarks, but harsh is broader, adding general severity and quick judgment beyond tart's sharp verbal edge.")
  Gloss: This means speaking in a sharp, cutting way, with a caustic edge to one's remarks that wounds more than it teases.
- **task-oriented** (`task_oriented#1`, cut-off 3) by [focused](../../../traits/instructions/focused.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve staying on the task and finishing it, but task-oriented adds breaking work into steps and cutting small talk and waste, while focused emphasizes resisting distraction and finishing one thing before the next."), Opus 3 ("Both describe keeping attention on the task and finishing it before moving on, but task-oriented adds breaking work into steps and driving for speed and efficiency, while focused centres on resisting distraction.")
  Gloss: This means keeping attention on the job at hand, breaking work into concrete steps, and driving each one to completion quickly without detours, small talk, or wasted effort.
- **tearless** (`tearless#1`, cut-off 3) by [stoic](../../../traits/instructions/stoic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve composure and restraint under pain, but tearless is specifically about not crying, while stoic is broader, adding rational detachment and philosophical acceptance."), Opus 3 ("Tearless is the stoic's emotional restraint applied specifically to grief and pain, while stoic is broader and adds philosophical acceptance, so they differ mainly in scope.")

- **temerarious** (`temerarious#1`, cut-off 4) by [reckless](../../../traits/instructions/reckless.json): Sonnet 3 ("Both mean heedless risk-taking with little concern for consequences; reckless is the common synonym, with a slightly broader description that includes not noticing the risks."), Opus 4 ("Both describe heedless risk-taking with disregard for consequences, and the two labels are near-synonyms.")

- **theistic** (`theistic#1`, cut-off 3) by [Muslim](../../../traits/instructions/muslim.json): Sonnet 2 ("Being Muslim is a specific religious identity that includes theistic belief plus particular practices, while theistic is the general belief in a god or gods; Muslim implies theistic but theistic doesn't imply Muslim, so they overlap with different scope and added content."), Opus 3 ("Being Muslim is a specific form of theism that adds particular beliefs and practices, so it entails theism, while theism does not entail being Muslim.")
  Gloss: This means holding that a god or gods exist and that belief in them is a settled part of how one understands the world and one's place in it.
- **thriftless** (`thriftless#1`, cut-off 3) by [extravagant](../../../traits/instructions/extravagant.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe spending beyond need and letting money run out, but thriftless stresses careless, unplanned waste while extravagant stresses lavish spending on the best and the most."), Opus 3 ("Both describe careless, wasteful spending that lets money go; extravagant adds an emphasis on lavishness and luxury, while thriftless stresses the lack of saving.")

- **thrilling** (`thrilling#1`, cut-off 3) by [animated](../../../traits/instructions/animated.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe lively, enthusiastic, vivid communication, but thrilling stresses energizing and mobilizing others while animated stresses expressive imagery and style, so they share a core with different emphases."), Opus 3 ("Both describe energetic, vivid, enthusiastic communication, but thrilling stresses energizing and mobilizing others while animated stresses lively expressive language and imagery.")

- **tight** (`tight#1`, cut-off 3) by [frugal](../../../traits/instructions/frugal.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve spending as little as possible, but 'tight' adds grudging, stingy refusal to spend on others, while 'frugal' is prudent economy without the reluctance or meanness, so they share a core yet each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Both are about minimizing spending, but tight adds grudging stinginess, especially toward others, while frugal is a neutral habit of thrift, so tight is frugality carried further with a negative tone.")
  Gloss: This means guarding one's money closely, grudging every expense, refusing to spend on others or on oneself, and counting each coin before parting with it.
- **tight-wad** (`tight_wad#1`, cut-off 3) by [frugal](../../../traits/instructions/frugal.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve minimal spending, but tight-wad adds grudging stinginess and reluctance to give or pay even when others do, while frugal is neutral or even prudent thrift focused on needs and making things last."), Opus 3 ("Both are about minimising spending, but tight-wad carries it further into grudging stinginess, even toward others, where frugal is simply careful thrift.")
  Gloss: This means refusing to spend money beyond the bare minimum, grudging every purchase and every gift, and keeping one's own cash tightly held even when others around one are paying.
- **timeless** (`timeless#1`, cut-off 3) by [steady](../../../traits/instructions/steady.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve constancy of character, but 'timeless' is about staying the same and never seeming dated across years and fashions, while 'steady' is about consistency of tone and view within a single conversation, so they overlap without either implying the other."), Opus 3 ("Both describe holding the same values, manner and view without swerving, differing mainly in scope: across years and fashions versus within a single conversation.")

- **tires easily** (`tires_easily#1`, cut-off 3) by [lethargic](../../../traits/instructions/lethargic.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve low physical energy and quick exhaustion, but lethargic adds a habitual slow, dragging pace of movement and speech, while tires easily is about low stamina and needing frequent rest, so each has something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both describe low physical energy. - **top-flight** (`top_flight#1`, cut-off 3) by [competent](../../../traits/instructions/competent.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe skill at one's work, but top-flight means elite, standout excellence while competent means reliably adequate and sound; same dimension at different degrees, though competent does not imply the elite standard."), Opus 3 ("Both describe skill at one's work, but top-flight is elite excellence while competent is solid adequacy; top-flight implies competent carried much further.")

- **tough** (`tough#1`, cut-off 3) by [resilient](../../../traits/instructions/resilient.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both describe withstanding adversity and continuing through setbacks, but tough stresses enduring without complaint while resilient stresses bouncing back and adapting, so they share a core and each adds something."), Opus 3 ("Both describe holding up under adversity; resilient adds bouncing back and adapting, while tough stresses steady endurance, so they differ mainly in emphasis.")

- **traditionalist** (`traditionalist#1`, cut-off 3) by [orthodox](../../../traits/instructions/orthodox.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve adhering to established ways and distrusting novelty, but orthodox is specifically about doctrine and authority and treating departures as error, while traditionalist is about customs generally, so each adds something the other lacks."), Opus 3 ("Both mean adhering to the established and resisting novelty; orthodox narrows this to doctrine and authority and pushes it further, treating any deviation as error.")

- **trifling** (`trifling#1`, cut-off 3) by [lighthearted](../../../traits/instructions/lighthearted.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve a light, joking, breezy manner toward serious matters, but trifling adds careless dismissiveness and disinterest in weighty subjects, while lighthearted is a more benign easy disposition."), Opus 3 ("Both describe treating even serious matters lightly and joking them off; trifling adds a more careless, dismissive edge, a difference of emphasis rather than concept.")

- **twinkly** (`twinkly#1`, cut-off 3) by [mischievous](../../../traits/instructions/mischievous.json): Sonnet 2 ("Both involve playful teasing and pranks, but twinkly is a light, glinting conversational manner, while mischievous adds rule-bending, disorder-sowing, and acting at someone's expense."), Opus 3 ("Both centre on playful teasing and pranks; mischievous carries it further into rule-bending and disorder at others' expense, while twinkly is a lighter, gentler version.")
